## 8. The definitional rules (classification 5.6)

Statement pass 7 (§6.2) runs after every verifying rule. It first computes each posted credit's payer facts (channel family, payer region, payer name, payer key, entry fields, and the hold predicates of §8.1). Then it runs Q7's credit-union arm (§8.7), the asset-sale reading (Q11 (2026-10-02) (b), §8.1) and the Q5 and Q6 verifications (§8.5, §8.6), which refuse any row a hold of §8.1 names or the asset-sale reading reads. Last, it gives every remaining `unverified_deposit` its tier and reason, in the order of §8.10.

### 8.1 Holds that apply to any channel

Every hold below skips a row that the registry, a payout entity or a factoring payee claimed (§8.9), except `insurer_payer`, `possible_return` and the pay and benefit holds, which read wording no platform prints on its own payouts. The **posting labels** removed before a hold reads a row are §7.5's credit posting labels, plus `INSTANT CREDIT`, `REAL TIME CREDIT`, `COUNTER CREDIT`, `POS CREDIT`, `ATM CREDIT`, `TELLER CREDIT`, `BRANCH CREDIT`, `CARD CREDIT`, `BATCH CREDIT`, `MERCHANT CREDIT` and `CREDIT FROM`, and the channel phrases `FUNDS TRANSFER`, `FUNDS AVAILABLE` and `INSTANT FUNDS`.

- **`insurer_payer`:** a row whose revenue method is `insurer_customer_payment` (§6.1 step 5, T14). The customer-payment wording, read on a credit from a listed insurer, is `\b(?:DRP|VENDOR ?(?:PMT|PAY|PAYMENT)|COMM?ISS?IONS?|AGT ?COMM|AGENT COMP|AGTEFT|REPAIR)\b`. Since the underwriter's Q2 (2026-10-02, R2-OW08) only a customer-payment row the for-work release refuses reaches it (premium- or refund-coded, under $1, a direction conflict, claimed); the rest pay for the business's work (below).
- **`insurer_named_payer`** (new): the payer region prints `\bINSUR\w*`, `\bASSURANCE\b`, `\bMUTUAL\b`, `\bCASUALTY\b`, `\bINDEMNITY\b` or `\bUNDERWRIT\w*`, or `\bCLAIMS?\b` on a row that is neither an `HCCLAIMPMT` entry nor from a healthcare payer. It closes Q6's "insurers never count" for carriers no registry lists (`FABRIKAM MUTUAL INSURANCE COMPANY DES:CLAIM PAYMT`). Measured on the memo's rows: $1.06M, 527 rows, 61 statements.
  Audit I26 (by Q6 of 2026-09-28, "insurers never count", and the last sentence of the underwriter's Q2 (2026-10-02) option the owner picked, "a one-off claim paid to a business on its own policy stays out"; the Q2 question did not ask it; §19.1, §20, R2-OW07): the reading (`insurer_payer_reading`) covers every insurer spelling, read on the payer region without the holder's own names (each of the holder's names by its runs, then R2-B04's other business names of the holder and the statement's receiver-field holder names, whole), so the holder's own `INSURANCE` word never makes its payer an insurer. Beside the spelled-out words above it reads the `INS` abbreviation; the cut forms `ASSUR`, `MUTUA`, `CASUALT…` and `INDEMN…`; `ASSURANCES`, `ASSURANT` and `ASSUREUR(S)`; `P AND C` (or `P & C`) at a name's end or before `INS…`, `CO`, `COMPANY` or `CORP`; `LOSS PMT`, `LOSS PAYMENT`, `LOSS PYMT` and `LOSS DRAFT`; `SUBRO…` (`SUBRO` and its cut forms `SUBROG…`, never the given name `SUBROTO`; R2-OW07 review round 1) (`_INSURER_SPELLINGS`); and the registry's `INSURER_CREDIT_BRANDS`, carriers that print no insurer word, each bounded as a whole name (Farmers, never `FARMERS IN BLOOM` or `FARMERS EXCHANGE BANK`; American Family, never `AMERICAN FAMILY CARE` or a dental practice; Safeco; Hiscox; Aflac; Gainsco; AmTrust, never its bank, title or realty namesakes; National General, never `NATIONAL GENERAL CONTRACTORS`; Travelers' indemnity, casualty, property and commercial lines and its agents' `PI COMM`, never `TRAVELERS CASH`), credit-only: no classifier rule, debit, flag or lender reading reads the table, and no record carries it. R2-OW07 review round 1: a brand's and `P AND C`'s `INS` is the insurer word or its cut (`INS`, `INSU`, `INSUR…`), never another word's first letters (`FARMERS INSTITUTE`, `FARMERS INSTANT`, `NATIONAL GENERAL INSTRUMENTS`, `<NAME> P & C INSTALLATIONS`), and Travelers' property line reads only before an insurer word (`CAS`, `CASUALT…`, `INS`, `INSUR…`) or at the name's end, never a property manager (`TRAVELERS PROPERTY MANAGEMENT`). `ASSURED`, `ASSURE`, `P AND C FOODS`, `CLM`, `CLMS` and `CLMEFT` are never read, and `_INSURER_NAME` is unchanged. On a person-to-person rail only the spelled-out words and `CLAIM` read, as before I26 (R2-OW07 review round 1): a sender's surname or given name (`INTERAC E-TRANSFER FROM <NAME> MUTUA`, `VENMO … SUBROTO <NAME>`) or the rail's own word (`APPLE CASH INS`, instant) is no cut insurer, and a brand never reads a person's transfer. Accepted over-holds, held and reviewable (R2-OW07 review round 1; the patterns cannot tell them from an insurer): an ACH payer whose name ends in `MUTUA` (a 16-letter field's cut of `<NAME> MUTUAL` prints the same), National General's bare name (the same field cuts `NATIONAL GENERAL CONTRACTORS` to it), `P AND C` at a name's end or before `CO` or `CORP` (a company named by its initials) and the `INS` token before another word (`<NAME> HOME INS INSPECTIONS`). The first arm that reads wins: an `HCCLAIMPMT` entry is no insurer; a government payer (§7.6) is an insurer only by the spelled-out words above or `CLAIM` (never on a healthcare payer), read without the holder's names and never for work, the reading the hold made before I26 (R2-OW07 review round 1: a government insurance programme's credit, employment, parental, disability or family-leave insurance or a public insurer's, `GOVERNMENT OF CANADA EMPLOYMENT INSURANCE`, `STATE OF <NAME> DISABILITY INSURANCE`, `DEPT OF INSURANCE`, stays held and never counts as the business's work, a personal government benefit being never revenue under the MCA principle; the widened spellings and the brands never read a government payer); a listed insurer's credit (§6.1 step 5's `insurance_provider_credit_exclusion` or T14's `insurer_customer_payment`) is the registry's entity, never this hold (a premium financier none); a title firm is a title insurer when an insurer word or spelling prints (held here, as before; never for work); a premium-finance wording is premium financing, no insurer; a healthcare payer is an insurer only by the spelled-out words (Q6c unchanged: `AETNA LIFE INS … PREM` keeps its refusal); a §15 deferred payer (§7.7) only by those words or `CLAIM`; then a brand, keyed by its entity (a carrier `INSURANCE_PROVIDER_ALIASES` also names keeps that entity's name, `Travelers`, so one carrier is one key however it prints); then a spelled word, a spelling or `CLAIM`, keyed by the payer key. `CLAIM` is still read, never on an `HCCLAIMPMT` entry or a healthcare payer. A credit so read is held as `insurer_named_payer` exactly as the same credit spelled `INSURANCE` was, before the pay hold (`FARMERS INS DES:PAYROLL` is held here, not as `payroll_or_salary`), and a Q5 or Q6 repeat it now holds is the census's declared `q5_q6_held_insurer` (§14.2, §20). R2-OW07 review round 1: R2-OW06's precedence, an insurer-name hold other than IAA's keeping an asset sale held, reads this whole reading, so a payer the widened spellings or a brand read printing a truck, vehicle or equipment sale (`<NAME> INS CO DES:TRUCK SALE`, `SAFECO DES:VEHICLE SALE`) is held `insurer_named_payer`, not `non_revenue` `asset_sale_proceeds`, as the spelled-out insurer's already was (an insurer buying a vehicle reads as a total-loss settlement; held is reviewable); and a row whose only insurer reading was the holder's own name, read away by the holder strip, is counted where no later hold of §8.10 names it (Truist's `CREF <payer> <holder's cut name> CUSTOMER ID`, the holder test not reading the holder's name in the middle of the region: a payer printing no insurer word, T21, or a glued one, `<NAME>INSURANCE`; held before I26), while a later hold that names it holds it (`holder_name` where the holder test reads the name at the region's end).
  A reading the underwriter's Q2 release counts as paid for the business's work (below) is no longer this hold's.
- **Insurers paid for the business's work (Q2 (2026-10-02); `insurer_paid_for_services`, R2-OW08).** The underwriter answered Q2, "True revenue" (option 2): an insurer's credit is counted in True, flagged, never Verified and never toward a Q5 or Q6 repeat, when it pays the business for its work. Before the payer facts (as audit fix batch B3's processor release does), pass 7 re-states such a credit (`_insurer_for_work`) as an unverified deposit of method `insurer_paid_for_services` (rule `insurer_paid_for_services`, confidence 0.60, its reason naming the ground in words, never the payer's), unclaimed: the method never joins `_REGISTRY_METHODS` or any claimed set, so the insurer-name hold passes over it and every later hold of §8.10 (4 to 11) still reads it, and where none names it the tier is `counted_flagged` / `insurer_paid_for_services`.
  - **Eligible.** The insurer reading above (`insurer_payer_reading`, on the payer region the facts read) is for work (never a title insurer's or a government payer's); no registry, payout entity, factoring payee or financier claimed the row (the insurer-name hold's convention); it is $1 or more, its direction agrees, and it is an unverified deposit or the insurance rule's `non_revenue` (`insurance_provider_credit_exclusion`), never a row a classifier rule verified (a descriptor, a remittance). A premium, refund, return, dividend, cancellation, unearned, overpayment, member or subscriber word, or a personal benefit's (`DISAB…`, `INVALIDIT…`, `ANNUIT…`, `PENSION…`; the MCA principle), on the payer (read without the holder's names) or the purpose refuses every ground, unless a commission form prints in the same words (`PREM COMM`). The purpose is a wire's purpose fields (`_title_purpose_text`: OBI, RMR, PMT DET, RFB, URI; never its `REF`, which on the Fedwire layout is the sending bank: `REF COMM BANK NYC`) or the entry fields, read with R2-B12's layout entry (`_layout_entry`).
  - **Grounds, the first that applies.** (1) `holder_trade:<trade>`: a holder name (the holder's names, R2-B04's other business names of the holder, the statement's receiver-field holder names) reads a repair shop (`AUTO BODY`, `BODY SHOP`, `BODY WORKS`, `COLLISION`, `REBODY`, `PAINT AND BODY`, `AUTO REPAIR`, `AUTO GLASS`, `GLASS REPAIR|SHOP|SERVICE`, `REPAIR(S)`, `CARROSSERIE`, `DEBOSSELAGE`, `MECANIQUE`), an insurance agency (`INSUR…`, `ASSURANCE(S)`, `INS`, `UNDERWRIT…`), a clinic (`CLINIC…`, `MEDICAL`, `MED`, `HEALTHCARE`, `DENTAL`, `PHYSIO…`, `CHIRO…`, `THERAP…`, `OPTOM…`, `HOSPITAL`, `NURSING` and the like) or a pharmacy (`PHARMAC…`, `DRUG(S)`, `APOTHECARY`, `RX`, `CHEMIST`, `COMPOUNDING`): a strict word names the trade from one credit; a loose word (`AGENCY`, `AGENCIES`, `AGCY`, `BROKER(S)`, `BROKERAGE`, `COURTIER(S)`; `HEALTH`, `VISION`, `WELLNESS`, `SPEECH`, `OCCUPATIONAL`, `IMAGING`, `COUNSEL…`; `TOWING`, `RESTORATION`, `ROOFING`, `MITIGATION`) only on a statement with two or more eligible insurer credits, so it never counts a one-off; `HEALTHY`, `SURGE` and a bare `GLASS` are no trade word. (2) `service_form`: the payer and purpose words print the form insurers pay those trades with (`DRP`, `AGENT(S) EFT`, `AGTEFT`, `AGT COMM`, `AGENT COMP`, `COMM(S)`, `COMMISSION(S)`, `CONTINGEN…`, `PICOMM`, `REPAIR(S)`, `VENDOR PMT|PAY|PAYMENT`), or the row before its receiver fields prints the classifier's own customer-payment wording (for layouts that print it before the payer: `MTH AGTEFT <carrier>`; never a bare `COMM`). (3) `same_insurer_3_in_31_days`: one insurer key pays three or more eligible credits within an inclusive 31-day span (date[i+2] - date[i] ≤ 30 days; the span slides, so it reaches across a calendar month's edge: 03-01 to 03-31 holds, 03-01 to 04-01 does not; an undated credit counts as inside). The key is the registry's or the brand's entity, so one carrier is one key however it prints (`TRAVELERS INSURANCE` and `TRAVELERS INDEMN` pool), otherwise the payer key. (4) `insurer_service_statement`, only with the owner's switch `INSURER_FOR_WORK_STATEMENT_ARM` on (off: the literal reading, §17.1): another insurer's eligible credit on a statement where some key is frequent. A credit with no ground stays out as before: a listed insurer's stays `non_revenue`, any other is held (`insurer_payer` or `insurer_named_payer`): "a one-off claim paid to a business on its own policy stays out".
  - **What the release reads around it.** The insurer's `CLAIM` on a released row is no non-sale word (the release read it as a claim paid for the work: a body shop's, an agency's or a provider's claim payments); every other non-sale word still holds it. A released row is no insurer to B4's bill clause (`CounterCredit.insurer` False, applied on R2-B02's `CounterCredit`), so a one-off premium bill to the same carrier at another amount does not hold it, while a debit for its own amount or a recurring one still does (`payer_also_debited`). Its later holds, Q11's asset-sale reading (an IAA seller payout three times a month at a non-dealer is `non_revenue` / `asset_sale_proceeds`) and Q3's Zelle step (a Zelle credit from an insurer is `zelle_excluded`, its release kept as `zelle_prior_reading`) run as before; Q10's premium-trust hold, when it lands, holds it too. HCCLAIMPMT keeps verifying, a healthcare payer keeps Q6c, a §15 deferred payer is read only by the spelled-out words or `CLAIM` (§7.7), and the census declares the release (§6.3 narrowing 13; the demotion `insurer_paid_for_services`).
- **`possible_return`:**
  - `\bRETURN(?:ED|S)?\b`, `\bADJ(?:USTMENT|USTED)?\b`, `\bDISPUTE[DS]?\b`, `\bCREDIT MEMO\b`, `\bOVERPA\w*`, on a row the reversal rule did not claim;
  - a `DEBIT CARD CREDIT` or `POS CREDIT` row released from the reversal rule (§7.11) that no form and no single-row registry context verified;
  - audit fix batch B3 (§20): a card credit printed first (`CARD CREDIT`, `CARD CREDIT <merchant>`) with no push or person-to-person rail, and, as a backstop, step 3's 5.6 return, correction and refund spellings.
- **`financing_named_payer`** (T4). The financing roots are read, after the posting labels are removed, on:
  - the payer region (§5.2), read before D11's filtering, so `CAPITAL ONE …` keeps `CAPITAL`;
  - the entry fields (§5.2): `DES`, `CO ENTRY DESCR`, a wire's `OBI` and purpose text, and a memo;
  - on a row with no payer region (a check, cash, branch, ATM or bare row), the row before its receiver fields.

  A run that equals the holder's whole normalized `account_name` (two or more words) is removed first, so a label-less receiver field never supplies a root; audit fix batch B7 (I47, §20): so is a run of its first two words or more, with the legal form printed or left off, when the account name names the holder (a company form or a person's name, never a product name such as `BUSINESS REWARDS CHECKING`). Audit round 2, R2-B04 (R19, R40, §20): the holder's name names the holder also with a trailing `CO` after two words or more or Quebec's `S.E.N.C.` (a city and state such as `SAMPLEVILLE CO` still names nobody), when a side of a `DBA`, `AKA` or BMO's `Operating as:` name names it, and with a leading `THE` or a partnership's `AND` (or `&`) read as no word of the name (a name of five words or more with no form still names nobody); the runs of each such side are removed too, and a run's last word of five letters or more cut by the bank's field to four letters or more at the row's end (`NORTHWIND DISTRIBUTIO`, `NORTHWIND DISTRIB`); and so is every business name of the holder's, never a person's: beside the holder's name, the account-name field's business when the holder hold reads it as a second name (a parser's holder name `JOHN SAMPLE` beside the account name `NORTHWIND CAPITAL LLC`) and reads as no person's name, and the trade side of a `DBA` name always, its legal side when it prints a company form (`JOHN SAMPLE DBA NORTHWIND PAYROLL SERVICES` adds `NORTHWIND PAYROLL SERVICES`, whose `SERVICES` keeps the side from naming a holder by itself); a person-shaped account-name field beside the parser's holder name (an owner's or a co-owner's name) is never added, so that person's pay from another company stays held (Q8). A whole-word `CREDIT` counts as a root only inside a payer name, next to another name word (`UNITED AUTO CREDIT`, `CREDIT ACCEPTANCE`, `FABRIKAM CREDIT UNION`); in an entry field and on a row with no payer region, a standalone `CREDIT` is a posting word and is never read (BofA's `COUNTER CREDIT`, `DES:CREDIT`). Glued, it always counts (`BIZ2CREDIT`, `CREDITLINE`). Audit fix batch B7 (I16, §20): the plural `CREDITS` is a statement's section word (`DEPOSITS AND CREDITS`, `OTHER CREDITS`), never a root, whole or glued, except (B7 review round 1, §20) before a company form after another name word in a payer region (`<NAME> CREDITS LLC`), where it is a lender's name word as `CREDIT` is; and a whole-word `CREDIT` that ends the payer region after a single letter is the entry word a layout prints after an originator name its field cut (`<NAME> P CREDIT`).

  Audit fix batch B7 (I16, §20; the roots are read only on text that can name the payer): a cash, branch, ATM or check deposit with no payer region prints its location (`… DEPOSIT 123 GLENDALE AZ`, `… CAPITAL BLVD …`, `ATM DEPOSIT <NAME> FIN CU <street>`), so no root is read on its location (Q2, Q3): B7 review round 1 (§20), its branch's label (`<NAME> FIN CTR`, `… FINANCIAL CENTER`), its credit union's name (`<NAME> FIN CU`, `… CREDIT UNION`, `… FCU`) and a street's name are removed, and what is left is read for whole financing words only (a word that starts with a financing word, `CREDIT` aside, or a whole-word root; never a root inside a word, such as a town's name), so a funder's name printed on the deposit (`MOBILE DEPOSIT <NAME> FUNDING LLC`, `COUNTER CREDIT <NAME> MERCHANT FUNDING`) still holds; B7 review round 2 (§20): the deposit's bank (the statement's own, a listed sending bank), a place a suffix names (`PLAZA`, `MALL`, `CIR`, `CIRCLE`, `CTR`, `CENTER`, `CENTRE`, `SQ`, `SQUARE`, `DISTRICT`, `HEIGHTS`, `PARK`), up to two words before `BRANCH`, and a town of one or two words before a state's code that ends the row or comes before a ZIP, a reference, a country or `ON <date>` (never a company form; `CO` is a company form there, never Colorado's code) are its location too, and a buyer's advance purchase or payment (`ADVANCE TICKET SALES`, `ADVANCE PAYMENT`) and a hold notice's `FUNDS` or `FUNDED` (`FUNDS ON HOLD`, `FUNDS AVAIL NEXT DAY`; still read before a company form, `<NAME> FUNDS LLC`) are never read, so `ATM DEPOSIT <n> ADVANCE NC`, `… CAPITAL HEIGHTS MD`, `1 FINANCIAL PLAZA`, `COUNTER CREDIT CAPITAL CITY BRANCH` and a Capital One ATM on a Capital One statement are counted; audit round 2, R2-B13 (R35, §20; B7 review round 3, minor 1): such a place, branch name or town that holds a financing word the reading keeps is removed only when that word is its first word and its only one and the token right before it is the row's start, a token with a digit or a mask, one of the deposit's own words (`DEPOSIT`, `DEP`, `DEPOSITS`, `DEPOSITED`, `EDEPOSIT`, `ATM`, `ABM`, `BRANCH`, `BRCH`, `BR`, `COUNTER`, `CREDIT`, `TELLER`, `CASH`, `CHECK`, `CHECKS`, `CHEQUE`, `MOBILE`, `REMOTE`, `ONLINE`, `IN`, `AT`; R2-B13 review round 1, §20: and `STORE` right after `BRANCH`, Wells Fargo's own `DEPOSIT MADE IN A BRANCH/STORE`, never `STORE` alone), a word inside §8.3's check-deposit form or §8.2's cash, branch or ATM form (Wells Fargo's `ATM … DEPOSIT ON <date> <address> <town> <ST> <n> ATM ID …`, `NIGHT DROP <place>`), or the street suffix that ends a numbered address (`<n> MAIN ST CAPITAL HEIGHTS MD`), so a funder's name printed before a location (`MOBILE DEPOSIT <NAME> FUNDING <town> <ST>`, `… <NAME> CAPITAL PA`, `… <NAME> CAPITAL PLAZA`, `DEPOSIT <NAME> CAPITAL CITY BRANCH`, `COUNTER CREDIT <NAME> LENDING PARK`) still holds while those places count; on every row a bank's branch label after a bank's name (`BOFA FIN CTR`, `… FINANCIAL CENTER`), the banks' page furniture (`MEMBER FDIC`, `EQUAL HOUSING LENDER`), a fundraising purpose (`FUNDRAIS…`) and Wave Payments' payout entry (`WAVE <code> FUNDIN WAVE`, `WAVE FUNDING INSTRU…`) are removed first; on a person-to-person rail row the sender's bank (a listed sending bank, the statement's own bank, a credit union's name before `CREDIT UNION` or `FCU`) is removed, and a sender that reads as a person's name (two to five words of letters, no company form, no holder-noise, business or institution word, no whole-word root and no word starting with a financing word: `TRUE FINANCE`, `FAST FUNDING` stay read) is not read, so a root inside a surname holds nothing (Q4); on a wire's purpose text a buyer's `ADVANCE PAYMENT`, `ADVANCE PMT` or `PREPAYMENT` for goods is removed (Q5). A memo that says funding (`ZELLE … FOR FUNDING`), a sender whose own name carries a root, and an ACH entry's `ADVANCE PMT` still hold. Customers whose own names carry a root (`ADVANCED …`, `… FINANCIAL`), a lessor's `LEASE` rent and lenders paying for services were left for the owner's ruling on audit I16, which the underwriter's Q9 of 2026-10-02 gave (the Q9 release below; R2-OW09). Audit round 2, R2-B09 (R06, §20): a layout's posting or channel label that prints `CREDIT` (`EDI EFT CCD CREDIT`, `INTERNET CREDIT`, `PREAUTH CREDIT`, `HIP CREDIT RCVD FROM`, `AVIS DE CREDIT`, `AUTOMATED CREDIT`) is a template prefix (§5.2), so it is never in the payer region and never a lender's name word; nor is the ACH entry `CREDIT NONE` ending the payer region after a cut name (`<NAME> CREDIT NONE`, as `<NAME> P CREDIT`), nor a credit union's `DIVIDEND CREDIT` (a dividend: held as `non_sale_purpose`). A lender named after the label (`PREAUTH CREDIT <NAME> ADVANCE LLC`, `ACH CREDIT <NAME> CREDIT CORP`), a credit union's own cut name as the originator (I16, with the owner) and Capital One's name stay held.

  The roots: `(?:FUND|CAPIT|CAPTL|LOAN|LEND|FINANC|ADVANC|MORTG|ACCEPTANCE|SERVICING|SERVICER|LEASING|PORTFOL)`, `CRED(?=ORA|IBLY)`, `CREDIT` glued on either side, or the whole words `CAP`, `CAPI`, `FIN`, `FINA`, `FINAN`, `FINL`, `FNCL`, `ADV`, `MTG`, `MCA`, `RTR`, `SPE`, `SPV`, `LEASE` (audit fix batch B6, §20: `SPE`, a special-purpose entity). `FACTOR` is not a root: a factor's payout is revenue (owner, 2026-09-26), and registered factors are decided before this pass. A glued `FINUSA` is not a root (B6 review round 1, §20): with no left boundary it read any run-together payer name ending in `FIN` + `USA` (a muffin or griffin brand, `<NAME>FINUSA LLC`), held even as a Q6 repeat; Forward Financing's run-together `FORWARDFINUSA` is its ledger alias, read with a reference glued on (§6.1 step 6).

  **The Q9 release (owner ruling 2026-10-02, the underwriter's Q9, "Keep them as true revenue", option 2; audit I16, I36(d); R2-OW09).** T4's root arm is lifted for three kinds of row, each counted and flagged, never Verified and never toward a Q5 or Q6 repeat (`finance_named_release`, read in the payer facts on an unverified credit nothing claimed; `CreditFacts.q9`):
  - **Read by place.** Only the root arm (`financing_named`) is lifted, read place by place (`_financing_root_places`, financing_named's own reading: the payer reading, the entry reading, or a payer-less row's reading, each where a root fires; a special payer arm, the whole-word or formed `CREDIT`, a glued `…CRED` name or a wire's wrap-split root, is marked and no longer ends the reading, so an entry root beside it is seen). Every other financing arm still holds, in its order: the registry's financing, an unadmitted listed auto lender, a dealer-funding word, a lone credit union's `VHCL PURCH`, a bank-originated wire and a lending bank. A released row takes every later hold (`payer_debited_as_lender`, `holder_name`, `payroll_or_salary`, `personal_income`, `non_sale_purpose`, `payer_also_debited`, the payroll-tax hold, the $1 floor), and the insurer and possible-return holds come before it.
  - **Never released:** a line whose row before its receiver fields (the holder's names removed) prints `PROCEEDS` or a disbursement (`DISBURS…`).
  - **(a) `finance_named_customer` and (c) `lender_paid_for_services`:** the root fires on the payer's name alone (no entry or row place) and the line prints §7.5's accounts-payable, vendor-payment or invoice wording (`_accounts_payable_wording`, the holder's names removed) or `COMMISSION(S)` (the orchestrator's extension under the underwriter's Q10, "commissions that reach the agency's operating account"; not Q9's own words). Never a payer region that names only a bank (R2-B03's `_bank_only_payer`). The payer's name reading as a lender's (`_LENDER_NAME_WORD`: a funding, lending, loan, capital, cash-advance, advance, MCA, acceptance, servicing, finance, mortgage, credit, leasing or portfolio word, `FINANCIAL` and `ADVANCED` left out; or a listed auto lender originating the row, `DEALER_FUNDING_PAYERS`) labels the row (c), `lender_paid_for_services`; every other payer is (a). The label is a label only: a customer whose name starts with a whole-word `ADVANCE`, `CAP`, `ADV` or `CREDIT` (`ADVANCE AUTO PARTS`) is labelled (c), its tier the same.
  - **A layout with no entry label** (empty entry fields: Wells Fargo, Citizens, TD and others print the entry words inside the payer region): a payer reading with two or more roots, or a root at or after the end of its first company form (`LLC`, `INC`, `CORP`, `CO`, `LTD` …), stays held (`_labelless_root_refusal`: `<NAME> CAPITAL ADVANCE VENDOR PMT`, `<NAME> LLC FUNDING PAYABLES`). A single root such a layout prints cannot tell a name from a purpose and is read as the name (the owner's (a)): `<NAME> FUNDING PAYABLES` is released whether `FUNDING` is the payer's name or the purpose's.
  - **A payer-less row** (a check, cash or deposit row with no payer region, or a transfer read on the whole row): its root is read on the whole row, so (a) and (c) never release it; a finance-named customer's check with an invoice memo stays held.
  - **(b) `lessor_rent`:** the statement's business is in leasing or property (`_lessor_business`), no special payer arm fired, and every place that fired is the rent sense of `LEASE` alone (`_RENT_LEASE`: never before `FUND…`, `FINANC…`, `LOAN`, `ADVANCE`, `PROCEEDS`, `BUYOUT`, `PURCH…` or `TO OWN`; the `LEASING` root is no rent), no other root left once it is blanked. A payer place is a rent memo only after the payer's first company form, with no root before the form's end (`<NAME> LLC LEASE PMT`, a memo the region swallowed): a payer named `LEASE …` before its form (`LEASE HOLDINGS LLC`) is no memo. A lease-to-own fund (`LEASE FUND`) and a leasing company stay with Q8 and T4.
  - **The lessor** (`_lessor_business`, read once per statement in pass 7 beside the business shape and the disbursers): one of the holder's names (the first credit's holder names, its account name and its holder name) prints a leasing or property trade word (`_PROPERTY_TRADE`: `REALTY`, `REAL ESTATE`, `PROPERTY`, `PROPERTIES`, `PROPS`, `LEASING`, `RENTAL(S)`, `LANDLORD`, `APARTMENT(S)`, `APTS`, `LOFTS`, `TOWNHOMES`, `STORAGE`, `PARKING`, `PLAZA`, `MALL`, `ESTATES`, `PROP MGMT`); or a property-management platform's credit posts (§7.10, `property_management_payments`); or two or more distinct payers pay rent: non-duplicate posted credits that no non-revenue rule took, no card credit and no Zelle deposit (Q3 (2026-10-02) excludes it later in the pass; the skip is kept in both readings of the owner's amendment of 2026-10-06 to the underwriter's Q3, so the Zelle setting moves Zelle rows only, R2-OW17), printing `RENT`, `RENTS`, `RENTAL(S)` (never `RENT A CAR`) or a rent `LEASE` on the row before its receiver fields, the holder's names removed; a row with a payer region counts under its payer key unless the region names the holder; a payer-less row counts as its own payer only on a check, cash, branch or ATM deposit; a payer-less transfer, person-to-person or wire row is never a rent payer.
  - **The hidden-loan guard, last:** a payer the statement debits stays held as `financing_named_payer` (`_payer_collects`, R2-OW05's: any lender or other posted debit naming the payer by the B4 forms, 5.6's first word or a cut or glued spelling; only the bank's receiving fee and a card purchase are ignored). This is a documented over-hold of the owner's "collecting loan payments": a bill or a fee the business pays the same payer holds it too.

Audit fix batch B4 (§20: I02, I38, I56) narrows it to the debits that can be circular money, as its purpose states: the bank's own receiving fee for an incoming wire or funds transfer never holds the payer; a processor's own fee, discount, chargeback, adjustment or returns debit never holds a credit that prints settlement, payout, `MID` or merchant-services wording; a bill the holder pays (bill pay, EBPP, autopay, a utility, telecom, cable or subscription) never holds a payer that does not read as an insurer; except that a fee or bill debit for the credit's own amount, or a bill debit that is one of two or more at one amount, still holds (a processor's fixed fee recurs at one amount by nature). The debit's kind is read without its receiver fields' values, the holder's own name. A transfer, wire, person-to-person or own-account debit matches at any size. Generic words and banks' channel names never make the first word (`MERCHANT`, `EXPRESS`, `UTILITIES` …), a name glued on one side matches it spaced on the other, and a three-letter payroll provider (`ADP`) is a word. Review round 1: `FROM` before the holder's own account (an account word or a masked account number) or before `TO` starts no sender, so `WIRE TRANSFER FEE FROM CHECKING TO <payee>` is the fee for the holder's own wire; `OUTGOING`, `BNF` and `BENEFICIARY`, which no sender's name prints, are read after the sender too.

### 8.2 Q2: cash, branch, ATM and bare deposits; transfer wording

The patterns follow the memo's `categorize.py`, which agrees with 94% of 315 hand-sorted payer groups; every pattern that file holds is inlined below. The cash, branch and ATM patterns apply only to a row that prints no electronic-payment form and no person-to-person rail, so an ACH payer named like a branch (`BRANCH MESSENGER`) is never read as a teller deposit.
