- These three are `counted_flagged` / `no_payer_printed`, never Verified (§6.1 step 9b).
- **Two cash shapes the reader missed** (owner ruling 2026-10-02, the underwriter's Q7: "make cash injections like ATM count as true revenue"; R2-OW14, §20), each the cash form's own last alternative, so they join the three above (`counted_flagged` / `no_payer_printed`, never Verified; G10 covers them):
  - **Arm R, a retail cash load:** `(?<![A-Z])US ?(?:WALGREENS|CVS|7 ?ELEVEN|WAL ?MART|DOLLAR GENERAL|RITE ?AID|FAMILY DOLLAR|CIRCLE K) W ?\d+$` (`_RETAIL_CASH_LOAD`), Bluevine's `<ST> <town> <street> US<RETAILER> W<n>` at the row's end. Inferred from the shape: no statement was opened to confirm it is a cash load at a retail cash network. The statements that carry it print the bank's `CASH DEPOSIT FEE` debits beside the loads (41 in the five statements with the corpus's 46 loads, 20 of them dated on a load's day), which reads as the fee for a retail cash deposit.
  - **Arm S, a branch deposit printed with its transit:** `^(?:\d{1,2} \d{1,2} )?DEPOSIT (?!.*\b(?:LLC|L L C|INC|INCORPORATED|CORP|CORPORATION|COMPANY|LTD|LTEE|LIMITED|LLP|PLLC|ULC|PLC)\b)(?:[A-Z]+ ){1,4}\d{5} \d{3}$` (`_BRANCH_DEPOSIT_TRANSIT`), Scotiabank's `DEPOSIT <place> <5-digit transit> <3-digit sequence>` as the whole row; a row that prints a legal form names a depositor and keeps its reading, and a card settlement printing digits right after `DEPOSIT` is no branch deposit. The arm reads any bank's row of that shape; the corpus has none outside Scotiabank.
  - A row of either shape prints no payer, so a same-place debit (a purchase at the store, a withdrawal at the branch) no longer holds it as `payer_also_debited`, and a branch deposit's place is no longer read as a named payer (`named_payer_unlabelled`).
- **Bare deposit, credit or EFT,** on any channel: after the template prefixes, `GENERIC_WORDS` and the reference tokens are removed, no payer word remains, and the row prints no transfer wording. It is `counted_flagged` / `no_payer_printed` too (§8.10, last step), never Verified. BMO's `DIRECT DEPOSIT <digits>` is a numbered company (§5.2) instead.
- **A payer the parser did not read** (audit fix batch B10: I05, I60, §20): Q2 covers a row whose statement prints no payer, never a row whose parser lost the payer the statement printed. A deterministic parser marks a credit it publishes with only its own posting-type or section label because it could not read the printed payer (`Transaction.payer_text_unread`: a core-processor merchant block the attribution count cannot give to one row, the daily core-processor template's every credit block while its reading waits on G7 (a teller's reference aside, which names no payer; audit fix batch B10 review round 1), First Citizens' `Other Credit` where its description overlay fails closed); such a row, where the pass would read it as a bare deposit (§8.10's last step), is `counted_flagged` / `payer_text_not_read` instead of `no_payer_printed`, never Verified. Every hold before it still applies (a marked bare transfer label stays `transfer_no_counterparty`), and a cash, branch, teller or ATM label keeps `no_payer_printed` marked or not, since the label itself says the statement printed no payer (B10 review round 1). Whether such rows should be held instead would change this section's rule and is the owner's; the statement carries the fact `payer_text_unread` when more than 30% of its posted credit rows are marked (§9.1). Audit round 2, R2-B07 (R07, §20): the counted core-processor template keeps, on each credit it marks at a welded flush, that flush's joined text (`Transaction.unread_payer_text`, §9.1), the blocks of every row outstanding at it; a marked row that would be `payer_text_not_read` is held as `unread_run_names_financing` instead when one block of that text (split after each ACH class code) names a registry lender of a lender or financing state other than an alternative position or a factor (§8.1, Q6: lenders never count) or a lending bank (`LENDING_BANK_CREDIT_PAYERS`, T4). The bare financing root is not read (a customer named `CAPITAL` stays `payer_text_not_read`), the text never verifies, never names the row's payer and never puts an amount toward lender credits, and the review card prints it so a reviewer can release a customer's row the lender's block held. Which row of the run is the lender's stays unknown: pairing blocks by printed order is not done (B10 measured out-of-order flushes).
- **Transfer wording:** `\bTRANSFER\b`, `\bTRNSFR\b`, `\bXFER\b`, `\bTFR\b`, `\bBR TO BR\b`, `\bONLINE BANKING\b`, `\bINTERNET (?:BANKING|TRANSFER)\b`, `\bFUNDS TRANSFER\b`, on a row that prints no person-to-person rail. Audit fix batch B8 (I46, §20): and the plural `\bTRANSFERS\b` (`EXTERNAL DEPOSIT ACH TRANSFERS PAYMENT`, `… FUNDS TRANSFERS`), now that §7.0's revenue text cuts TD's back panel, which prints `… ELECTRONIC FUNDS TRANSFERS`; the holds' posting labels drop `FUNDS TRANSFERS` as they drop `FUNDS TRANSFER`. Audit round 2, R2-B09 (§20): American Express's label `ONLINE TRANSFER PAYMENT CREDIT` at the row's start is no transfer wording only when an originator word follows it (R31: the bare label, or the label before `FROM`, an account word, `ID`, a masked account or digits, is a bare transfer, held); the glued `ONLINETRANSFER`, `MOBILETRANSFER` and `INTERNETTRANSFER` (singular or plural) are transfer wording, the glued label at the row's start under the same originator rule (R45); and on a credit, transfer wording printed inside a company-formed ACH originator's own name (before `DES`, after `ORIG CO NAME`: `CONTOSO TRF LLC`, `TRF INDUSTRIES INC`, `CONTOSO TRANSFER INC`) is the company's name, never a transfer, so the row is an ACH payer Q6 reads (R28); the entry field's wording (`DES:TRANSFER`, `CO ENTRY DESCR:BANK XFER`) is still read, and a name with no company form once the wording is out (`<NAME> BANK XFER`, `TRANSFER AND STORAGE CO`) keeps the transfer reading. A debit's reading and Q6's entry-field refusal are unchanged. R2-B09 review round 1 (§20): `DES` opens that name only with a field of Bank of America's layout after its entry (`ID`, `INDN`, `CO ID`, `IND NAME`, `IND ID` or an ACH class code), never as a town's word (`TRANSFER FROM <NAME> LLC DES MOINES IA`), and a name printing a transfer's phrase word (`FROM`, `FRM`, `FR`, `TO`, `BETWEEN`) is no company's own name: such a named transfer keeps its transfer reading.
  - With no counterparty (no payer word after the template prefixes, `GENERIC_WORDS`, the account words of T13 and the reference tokens are removed), it is `excluded_pending_review` / `transfer_no_counterparty`. The tier pass tests this **before** the check, cash, branch and ATM tiers, so `TELLER TRANSFER` is held, not counted.
  - With a named counterparty, T13 and §8.4 apply.
  - **In a package** (owner ruling 2026-10-02, the underwriter's Q4; R2-OW16): a debit printing transfer wording is the transfer out §6.2's package pass 2 matches a bare deposit of another of the business's accounts to (0 to 2 days, exact cents; package-only). Its paper-or-cash guard (`paper_or_cash_deposit`, read on the row before its receiver fields) refuses a check deposit (§8.3) and a cash, branch, teller or ATM form above that prints a cash device's word (`_CASH_DEVICE_WORD`: `ATM`, `ABM`, `CASH`, `COIN`, `SMART SAFE`, `CPS DEVICE`, `CURRENCY PROCESSING`, `NIGHT DEP…`, `NIGHT DROP`, `VAULT`, `PRE ENCODED`) or arm R's retail cash load: a paper item or cash is never a transfer's receiving leg. A teller, counter or branch deposit printing no such word stays eligible (a branch transfer between two of the business's accounts can print that way on its receiving side), and so does a bare `NIGHT DEPOSIT`, which the cash form above does not read (`NIGHT (?:DEP|DROP)` as whole words). Nothing here changes a statement's own reading.
- **A pull that names only a bank** (audit round 2, R2-B03: R05, §20; a bank's name is never the payer's name): an ACH or unlabelled credit whose payer region is only a listed sending bank's name (the registry's `P2P_SENDING_BANK_NAMES`, which now lists `MSPBNA` and `ALLY BANK`) or one to four words ending `BANK`, `BANCORP`, `FSB` or `CREDIT UNION` that read as a bank by its own form (never a food or blood bank, never a company whose name holds the bank word, never a bank's settlement form), a trailing `ACH`, `ONLINE` or `N A` aside, printed with no entry field, is the holder's pull from another of its own bank accounts (`ACH CREDIT <bank>` on Relay, `<bank> ACH` on Brex, `ELECTRONIC DEPOSIT FROM <bank>` on U.S. Bank): `excluded_pending_review` / `transfer_no_counterparty`, unless a rule verified it or the registry, a payout entity, a factoring payee or a factor claimed it. The statement's own bank's channel (`CHASE ONLINE` on a Chase statement) is never held: a customer's bill payment through the bank, counted with no payer (§8.6).

### 8.3 Q3: check deposits

`\bMOBILE (?:CHECK |CHEQUE )?(?:DEPOSIT|DEP)\b`, `\bMOBILE CHE(?:CK|QUE)\b`, `\bMB DEP\b`, `\bBKOFAMERICA MOBILE\b`, `\bREMOTE (?:ONLINE )?(?:DEPOSIT|CAPTURE)\b`, `\bDEPOSIT CAPTURE\b`, `\bMERCHANT CAPTURE\b`, `\bDESKTOP (?:REMOTE )?DEPOSIT\b`, `\bEDEPOSIT SCAN\b`, `\bE ?CHEQUE DEPOSIT\b`, `\b(?:ATM )?CHE(?:CK|QUE)S? (?:DEPOSIT|DEP|RECEIVED)\b`, `\bMAIL DEPOSIT\b`, `^REMOTE$`, `\bIMAGED DEPOSIT\b`, `\bDEPOSITED (?:CHECK|ITEM)\b`, `\bRDC\b`, `\bSCAN(?:NED)? DEPOSIT\b`, `\bLOCKBOX\b`, `\bLBX DEP\b`.

These are `counted_flagged` / `check_deposit`, never Verified (§6.1 step 9b). A returned deposited item is decided earlier, as a reversal.

### 8.4 Q4: person-to-person, and named transfers

- **Rails:** the consumer rails `\bZELLE\b`, `\bINTERAC\b`, `\bE ?TRANSFER\b`, `\bE ?TFR\b`, `\bVIREMENT\b`, `\bVFC\b`, `\bAUTODEPOSIT\b`, `\bVENMO\b`, `\bCASH ?APP\b`, `\bSQUARE CASH\b`, `\bAPPLE CASH\b`, `\bPOPMONEY\b`, and the real-time and push rails `\bREAL TIME (?:TRANSFER|PAYMENT)\b`, `\bRTP\b`, `\bFEDNOW\b`, `\bINSTANT (?:PMT|PAYMENT|TRANSFER)\b`, `\bVISA (?:MONEY TRANSFER|DIRECT)\b`, `\bMONEY TRANSFER\b`, `\bMC SEND\b`, `\bPMNT RCVD\b`, `\bPAYMENT RECEIVED\b`. A row the registry or a form already claimed (an RTP payout from Amazon, a Visa Direct payout from Square) is not a person-to-person row. Audit round 2, R2-B11 (R44, §20): a consumer rail whose reference is glued after its word (CIBC's `E-TRANSFER<reference> <sender>`) is read once the revenue text splits the digits off (§7.0), so Q4's holds reach it on every bank; B2's reason for keeping CIBC's glued rows off the rail (to keep them out of the round-sum hold) is withdrawn.
- **Named transfers** (T13): transfer wording (§8.2) with a named counterparty belongs here. Audit round 2, R2-B11 (R24, §20): a short own-account source after `FROM` (`CHK`, `CHECKG`, `CK`, `SAV`, `SV`, `MMA`, `DDA`, `PCA`, `CL`, `LOC`, `LN`, `CRD`) designates the holder's own account (§7.11 T5) only before an account number, a masked account, `ACCOUNT` or `ACCT`, or at the row's end; a company whose name starts with those letters (`TRANSFER FROM CL FABRIKAM INC`) is a named counterparty here (or a wire's sender, §8.5).
- **The sender** is the payer region (§5.2).
- **`transfer_account_designation`:** a named transfer whose row prints an account designation, an account-type word (`CHECKING`, `CHK`, `CHKG`, `SAVINGS`, `SAVING`, `SAV`, `SVGS`, `MONEY MARKET`, `MMA`, `DDA`, `ACCOUNT`, `ACCT`, `EVERYDAY`; audit round 2, R2-B09: R45, §20: and `CHCKING`, `CHKING`, `CKG`, which name no counterparty either) or a masked account number (`\bX{2,}\d{2,}\b`, `\bENDING (?:IN )?\d{3,}\b`), is held: it reads as the owner's account at another bank. Measured on the memo's rows: $1.18M, 1,473 rows, 168 statements.
- **`p2p_round_repeat`:** a sender with two or more round-sum credits on these rails or through named transfers in the statement has every one of its round-sum credits held. Its other credits stay counted. The memo counted a repeat of any amount; this reading follows the ruling's words, "repeated round sums from one sender".
- A sender with the holder's name is `holder_name` (§8.1).
- Everything else is `counted_flagged` / `p2p`, never Verified, even when the sender prints a company form (Q4, §6.1 step 9b).
- **Zelle (owner ruling 2026-10-02, the underwriter's Q3; a Settings choice since 2026-10-06):** the owner's amendment of 2026-10-06 to the underwriter's Q3 (R2-OW17, §19.1) makes it the Settings choice "Mark Zelle Payments as True Revenue", Yes by default. The analysis computes two readings of every statement that has a Zelle credit (`classify_statement_readings`: the shared prefix once, pass 7, pass 7b and the duplicate finalisation once per reading) and stores the first with the edits to the second (§9.1); the choice picks one when an analysis is shown, so nothing is reprocessed. **Yes, the counted reading** (`zelle_true_revenue=True`): the Zelle step below does not run, so each Zelle credit carries exactly the rules' own reading of a person-to-person credit (`p2p`, PNC's `ZEL FROM` as `named_payer_unlabelled`, or a hold: `holder_name`, `p2p_round_repeat`, `payer_also_debited`, `non_sale_purpose`, `financing_named_payer`, `possible_return`, `payroll_or_salary`), and every later step reads it as any row (the $1 floor, the premium-trust hold, the funding aid, pass 7b's returned funder payments). Two Q3-era carve-outs are lifted there: a builder's Zelle draw is a progress draw and a Zelle truck or equipment sale is asset-sale proceeds (§8.1), so such a row also leaves Q5's and Q6's repeats, as a Venmo sale or draw does (a repeat partner on its payer key can lose a verification: declared, §14.2). The lessor fact keeps its Zelle skip in both readings (§8.1), so the setting moves Zelle rows only. The latest decision on a Zelle row sets both readings (§10.7). **No, the stored reading:** every posted Zelle credit is `non_revenue` / `zelle_excluded` (method and rule `zelle_deposit_excluded`), whoever sent it, a lender or a processor paying through Zelle included. The rail reader (`zelle_deposit`) reads the revenue text before the receiver fields: `ZELLE` with no letter on either side (a glued date or reference reads: `ZELLE1234567`, `0302ZELLE`) or PNC's `ZEL FROM|TO`, never a name holding the letters (`HAZEL`, `ROSZELL`, `MAZZELLA`, `ZELLER`, `EZELL`). It is pass 7's last tier step (§8.10 step 26): a count, a verification and every hold (the round-sum repeat, the holder's name, a payer also debited, financing, a payer debited as a lender, the $1 floor's) become the exclusion, and the rules' own tier and reason stay on the record (the reason sentence names them, and the context signal `zelle_prior:<tier>:<reason>` keeps them: `zelle_prior_reading`). A row a non-revenue rule decided (a refund, a reversal, an opposite-direction pair, an own-account transfer, a listed funder's financing proceeds with the lender-credit exclusion, a non-operating credit) keeps that rule and no reason, and a direction conflict keeps its hold. Everything before the step still reads Zelle rows (the holds, Q5's and Q6's counts, a sender's named round sums: a sender's Zelle round sum still completes its group on another rail). The classifier's consumer rail (`_CONSUMER_P2P_RAIL`), the legacy classes, the lender fields and the debits are unchanged; the other rails keep this section's reading.

### 8.5 Q5: incoming wires

- **The wire family:** the leading labels of §7.9 N1, a third-party book transfer (§7.11, only with T19), or, for tiering only, the loose wire words `\bWIRE\b`, `\bFEDWIRE\b`, `\bFED WIRE\b`, `\bIWT\b`, `\bCHIPS CREDIT\b`, `\bSWIFT\b`, `\bFOREIGN REMITTANCE\b`, `\bWT FED\b`, `\bFED REF\b` on a row no rail of §8.4 claimed. Audit fix batch B5 (I14, I12's reader, §20): Navy Federal's `BANK WIRE DEPOSIT`, Columbia Bank's `WIRE DEPOSIT WIRE IN` and U.S. Bank's `WIRE CREDIT REF<n>` are N1 labels, and a loose-wire row's originator label (`ORIG`, `ORG`, `B O`, `ORIGINATOR`; never `ORIG CO` or `ORIG ID`) names its sender as an incoming wire's does. Audit round 2, R2-B10 (R26, §20): only a label printed after the row's first `WIRE` word, read from its own position; a label word before it is a word of the sender's own name on the `<sender> WIRE` layout (Mercury, Brex: `CONTOSO ORG LLC WIRE`, a `.org` domain), so the whole name is the payer region.
- **Verified: the same company twice or more** (method `repeat_wire_sender`, confidence 0.85). The row begins with an N1 label (or is a third-party book transfer under T19), and:
  - no hold of §8.1 applies to it;
  - its sender prints a company form (§5.2) or is a government or healthcare payer; audit fix batch B5 (I61, §20): here only, an `LLC` the 35-character originator field cut to `LL` and glued to the address after it (`<name> MANAGEMENT LL<city>`) is a company form; never a two-letter cut of another form (`CO`, `IN`, `LI`), and never for Q6;
  - two or more wire credits in the statement have that payer key (repeats, §5.2, which never count a held row);
  - the sender is not a numbered company (§5.2), and names no bank (`BANK`, `BANCO`, `BANCORP`, `N A`, `TRUST COMPANY`, `CREDIT UNION`, `FCU`, `SAVINGS`), since a relaying bank hides the real payer, and no title or escrow firm (`TITLE`, `ESCROW`, `CLOSING`, `SETTLEMENT`);
  - the row passes every veto of §7.9: the financing roots read as §7.9 reads them (after the channel words and the sending and intermediary bank fields are removed, and wrap-tolerant on the originator), the non-sale purposes, the own-account test, the brand-word affiliate test, the cut-field test and `match_known_payee`;
  - it prints none of the words that refuse a Q6 verification (§8.6).
- **Verified: an invoice or PO wire:** §7.9 (step 14).
- **Held:** a wire with no sender printed is `wire_no_sender` (audit fix batch B5, I14, §20: so is a wire whose sender region holds no name word, a lone glued reference, or only bank and layout labels: `BANK`, `DEPOSIT`, `INTERNATIONAL`, `IN`, `INCOMING`, `RECEIVED`, `DEP` and the bare channel words; `IWT` waits for audit batch B10; audit round 2, R2-B10 (R32, §20): the labels are the bare channel words, every wire layout word (`FEDWIRE`, `FED`, `INBOUND`, `INBD`, `CHIPS`, `SWIFT`, `WT`, `IWT`, `DOMESTIC`, `INTL`, `INTERNATIONAL`, `INCOMING`, `BOOK`, `TRANSFER`, `CREDIT`), `BANK`, `DEPOSIT`, `DEP`, `IN`, `RECEIVED` and `CR`, one list, so `INCOMING FEDWIRE`, `FEDWIRE CR` and `INBOUND WIRE` name no sender); one the holder test matches is `holder_name`; one whose sender is also debited in the statement is `payer_also_debited` (§8.1); one that a hold of §8.1 names takes that hold (`OBI SERIES A INVESTMENT`, `REF INTERCO SWEEP` and `OBI PAYROLL` are held). The underwriter's Q1 (2026-10-02; audit I12; R2-OW12): the hold stays, every no-sender shape included. Pass 7's last step (`funding_series_after`, after the $1 floor and the premium-trust hold, so it reads the final tiers) records on each held `wire_no_sender` credit every Lenders or Potential Lenders series that meets all of these: one tab name (the potential payee label, else the canonical entity, as the tabs list it) and one amount to the cent (find_recurring_debits' amount); posted, not a duplicate, counting toward the lender or potential-lender count (a settlement-reversed debit, whose counts the reversal pass cleared, is no payment); every row dated after the deposit's day, the first at most 10 days after it (`FUNDING_SERIES_WINDOW_DAYS`); two or more dates that `classify_cadence` reads daily or weekly (`_promotion_cadence` with `FUNDING_SERIES_MIN_PAYMENTS = 2`). `start_observed` says whether the statement shows a full gap of the series (its mean gap rounded up, and at least 3 days, `FUNDING_SERIES_MIN_LOOKBACK_DAYS`) before the deposit, counted from its printed period start, else from its earliest dated row. "Frequent payment" is read as a lender-side series (the Lenders or Potential Lenders tabs: registry funders, keyword recurrences, D6 payees), a narrowing of the ruling's "same payee or same amount" chosen on the measured noise: an all-debits pool is card purchases, payroll, own transfers and person-to-person payments. A registry lender's series needs two payments in the statement; an unknown payee is in the pool only once three fixed daily or weekly debits promote it (D6's and the keyword groups' promotion count). A series that follows several held wires goes on each, with its own days after. The aid never changes a tier, a reason, a figure or a lender row (G7: 0).
- **Otherwise:** `counted_flagged` / `wire_named_sender`, including senders that are persons, banks or title companies. A wire that §8.6's verification-only words refused is `named_payer_purpose_refused`.

### 8.6 Q6: named ACH and EFT payers

**Eligible rows** are unverified posted credits that meet all of these:
- the row prints an electronic-payment form (§5.2) and has a payer region;
- the channel gate (§6.1 step 9b) does not close it: it prints no person-to-person rail, and no transfer wording in its entry fields;
- it is not a wire;
- no registry alias, payout entity or factoring payee matched it, because platforms are decided by §7;
- no hold of §8.1 applies, so no financing root in its payer region or entry fields, no insurer name, no non-sale purpose, no pay wording and not the holder;
- it is not a numbered company (§5.2);
- audit round 2, R2-B03 (R05, §20): its payer region names more than a bank. A region that is only a listed sending bank's name, only the statement's own bank's name (its channel: `CHASE ONLINE` on a Chase statement) or one to four words ending in a bank's own form (§8.2's pull), a trailing `ACH`, `ONLINE` or `N A` aside, names no customer, so its repetition proves nothing; unless its entry prints a bank's merchant deposit or card settlement (`DEPOSIT`, `DEP`, `MTOT`, `BTOT`, `SETTLE…`, `STLMT`, `MERCH…`: `<bank> DES:DEPOSIT`, Synchrony's `MTOT DEP`) or its originator is a bank's settlement form, such a row is counted as `counted_flagged` / `no_payer_printed` (a bill payment through a bank, `<bank> … SEC:CIE`), or held by §8.2 when it prints no entry field.

**Refused** (counted as `named_payer_purpose_refused`, not verified, not held): a row whose entry fields or payer region print one of the verification-only words below. They are sales wording often enough that holding them would take real revenue out of True, but they are not proof: `\bSETTLEMENT\b` (a legal or insurance settlement prints it, and so does an unregistered processor), `\bTAX(?:ES)?\b`, `\bIRS\b`, `\bCRA\b`, `\bFEES?\b`, `\bSUBSCRIPTIONS?\b`, `\bDISCOUNT\w*`, `\bCOMM?ISS?IONS?\b`, `\bCOMPENSATION\b`, `\bEXPENSES?\b`, `\bAFFILIATE\b`, `\bPERSONAL\b`, `\bCLOSING\b`, `\bSCF\b`, `\bSUPPLY CHAIN\b`, `\bEARLY PAY(?:MENT)?\b`, `\bALLOWANCES?\b`, `\bSHORTAGES?\b`, `\bRMA\b`, and, in the entry fields only, `\bFLOOR ?PLAN\b`, `\bFLOORPLAN\b`, `\bVIN\b`, `\bEQUIP\w*`.

**Verified** (method `named_payer_repeats`, `named_payer_company_form` or `public_or_healthcare_payer`) when any of these holds:
- (a) the payer repeats (§5.2) and at least one of its credits is not a `PPD` or `WEB` entry. A consumer entry never verifies by repetition alone (structural S50);
- (b) the payer name prints a company form;
- (c) the payer is a government payer (§5.2, with §7.6's patterns and every veto) or a healthcare payer (§7.7) whose row prints none of `REIMB`, `MEMBER`, `MBR`, `SUBSCRIBER` or `PREMIUM`. Owner ruling 2026-10-02 (Q12): the seven no-purpose forms of step 3a (§6.1) are decided before arms A and B and before Q6; a purpose (`VENDOR PAY`, `PROV PAY`, `RMR IV`, a `PMT INFO` invoice, a VA entry code) keeps them here.

**Guard:** no posted debit in the same statement shares the payer's first distinctive word (§7.5). A payer that is also debited is held as `payer_also_debited`, and one debited as a lender is held as `payer_debited_as_lender` (§8.1).

**Otherwise** the row is `counted_flagged` / `named_payer_one_off`.

Lenders are decided `non_revenue` earlier (D1 and the potential registry), unregistered ones are held (T4), insurers are `non_revenue` or held (T14, `insurer_named_payer`), and the holder is held. That is Q6's "lenders, insurers and the holder never count," except an insurer paying for the business's work (§8.1, the underwriter's Q2 of 2026-10-02): counted and flagged, never verified and never a repeat.

### 8.7 Q7: an auto lender paying a dealer

At step 4 (§6.1), a credit is `verified_revenue` (method `auto_lender_dealer_funding`, source type `auto_dealer_funding`, confidence 0.90) when its payer, read on the originator segment (`_originator_segment`, never a receiver or memo field), is an auto lender, and one of these holds:
- **the listed-lender arms.** The payer is a listed auto lender: a `vehicle_financing` registry entity, or an entry of `DEALER_FUNDING_PAYERS` (registry, new: Westlake Financial (never Westlake Flooring), United Auto Credit, Strike Acceptance, PFS, Suncoast Credit Union, CU Direct / CUDL, Credit Acceptance, Exeter, Flagship Credit, GLS, Santander Consumer, Chrysler Capital, GM Financial, Toyota Financial, Honda Financial, Nissan Motor Acceptance, CarMax Auto Finance, Ally, American Credit Acceptance, Regional Acceptance, Nicholas Financial, Lendbuzz). And the row prints either:
  - dealer-specific funding words: `\bVHCL PURCH\w*`, `\bVEHICLE PURCHASE\b`, `\bDEAL ?FUND\w*`, `\bFUNDLOAN\b`, `\bDEALER (?:FUND\w*|FND|PMT|PAY\w*)\b`, `\bDLR PMT\b`, `\bAUTODLRPMT\b`, `\bCONTRACT FUND\w*`, `\bVADMIN FEE\b`; or
  - `\bPAYABLES\b`, `\bTRADE PAY\w*` or `\bACCT FUND\w*`.
- **the credit-union arm.** Credit unions fund dealers' indirect auto loans through CU Direct (CUDL) and print their own name with the entry `VHCL PURCH`. The payer region names a credit union (`\bCU\b`, `\bCREDIT UNION\b`, `\bFCU\b`) or CU Direct / CUDL; the entry field is `\bVHCL PURCH(?:ASE)?\b` (Chase's glued `VHCL PURCHSEC` is split by the revenue text, §7.0); and the statement holds two or more such credits. A single one can be a member's own purchase loan paid into the member's account, so it is held as `financing_named_payer`. Because it needs the statement, this arm is decided in statement pass 7 (§6.2), before the Q5 and Q6 verifications: step 4 leaves such a row `unverified_deposit` (method `credit_union_vehicle_purchase`), and the pass verifies it with method `auto_lender_dealer_funding` when the count is met. Audit fix batch B7 (I36, §20): a credit union's glued acronym (one to three letters before `CU` or `FCU`, one word: `BECU`, `SECU`, `PSECU`, `GECU`, `DCU`) names a credit union too; and once the arm verifies a statement's VHCL PURCH credits, the same credit union's other dealer-funding entries (its `VADMIN FEE`, the same deal's admin fee), or another credit union's entry that prints a verified credit's deal ID (Chase's `IND ID`), verify with them, under the same refusals; a credit union's entry beside no verified VHCL PURCH credit stays held.

Q7 never fires when any of these holds:
- the row matches a D1 entity outside the vehicle-financing group, a potential lender or an insurer (`KAPITUS DES:CONTRACT FUNDING`, `ONDECK CAPITAL DES:DEAL FUND`, `GEICO DES:VEHICLE PURCHASE`);
- the row prints `\bLOANS?\b`, `\bPROCEEDS\b`, `\bADVANCES?\b`, `\bADV\b`, `\bMCA\b`, `\bCASH ADV\w*` or a refund word (`REFUND`, `RFND`, `REFND`, `RFD`, `RETURN`, `RTN`, `REVERSAL`, `RVSL`, `CHARGEBACK`, `CHBK`) (`SUNCOAST CREDIT UNION DES:VHCL PURCH LOAN PROCEEDS`);
- the channel gate (§6.1 step 9b) closes the row.

**Payables need dealer evidence (owner ruling 2026-10-02, the underwriter's Q9 (c'); audit round 2, R2-OW05).** A listed lender's credit read on a payables word alone (PAYABLES, TRADE PAY, ACCT FUND) verifies only on a statement with dealer evidence: a Q7 credit with a dealer-specific word, or the credit-union arm; a floor-plan financier's row, or FLOOR PLAN; a purchase at a dealer-only auction; a dealer word in the holder's name, unless the name also prints RECOVERY, REPO, REPOSSESS, TOWING or COLLATERAL. Otherwise it is `counted_flagged` / `lender_paid_for_services` (Q9 (2026-10-02)), held under the hidden-loan guard. In detail:
- **The payables-only credit** (`_payables_only_dealer_funding`): step 4's listed-lender arm, whose word is a payables word, not a dealer-specific one (`dealer_funding_reading` reads a dealer-specific word first, so `PAYABLES DEALER PAY` is dealer-specific).
- **The dealer evidence** (`_dealer_contract_evidence`, read once per statement in pass 7, beside the business shape): the statement's dealer activity (`_dealer_activity`, the shared core R2-OW06's Q11 reads too): a credit of the statement that is a credit union's `VHCL PURCH` (verified by the credit-union arm or a lone one, method `credit_union_vehicle_purchase`) or a Q7 credit that is not payables-only; a posted row, credit or debit, of a floor-plan financier (classification `floor_plan_financing`, the registry's `FLOOR_PLAN_ALIASES`, or a `FLOOR PLAN` or `FLOORPLAN` form); a posted debit naming a dealer-only wholesale auction (`WHOLESALE_AUCTION_REFUND_NAMES`: Manheim, ACV Auctions, OPENLANE or BACKLOT CARS: a purchase there); or a dealer's name on one of the holder's names (a vehicle or equipment noun before `SALES`, `DEALER`, `DEALERSHIP`, `MART`, `OUTLET`, `EXCHANGE` or `SUPERSTORE`, or `MOTORS`, `AUTOMOTIVE`, `AUTO GROUP`, `AUTO PLAZA`, `AUTO MALL`, `DEALERSHIP`, `CAR LOT`) that prints no recovery, repossession, towing or collateral word. A payables-only Q7 credit is no dealer evidence (a repossession agency's own payables would make its statement a dealer's), nor is a §7.8 auction payout credit (it is Q11's evidence only).
- **The demotion.** In pass 7's tier loop, after the factoring, the holder's own push and the lease-to-own financier's demotions, a Verified payables-only Q7 credit on a statement with no dealer evidence leaves verification (`_lender_service_never_verified`: state `unverified_deposit`, method `lender_paid_for_services`, rule `q7_payables_without_dealer_evidence`, confidence 0.50, no source type; its reason names the lender and its alias, says the statement shows no dealer evidence and that the ruling overrules `auto_lender_dealer_funding`). It is `counted_flagged` / `lender_paid_for_services`, or `excluded_pending_review` / `financing_named_payer` when the lender also collects from the account.
- **The hidden-loan guard** (`_payer_collects`): a lender or financing debit names the payer (`payer_debited_as_lender`'s reading, with the pass-7 prefix), or any other posted debit names it by the B4 forms, 5.6's first word or a cut or glued spelling; only the bank's receiving fee and a card charge are ignored. It reads more broadly than `payer_also_debited` (no bill, processor-fee, settlement or payout-pair exemption, no amount or recurrence test): a documented over-hold of the owner's "collecting loan payments".
- **What stays.** The transaction side (classification `other`, match method `auto_lender_dealer_funding`, the lender's name and every lender flag) is unchanged, so lender credits and eligible deposits do not move; Q7's dealer-specific words, credit-union arm and vetoes are unchanged; a dealer's payables on a statement with dealer evidence stay Verified; a registered lender's other credits stay financing proceeds. A real dealer whose statement shows none of the evidence (no floor plan, no dealer-worded Q7 credit, no auction purchase and no dealer word in its name), or whose name prints RECOVERY or REPO, loses Verified but stays in True, flagged.
- **Q9's other parts (R2-OW09).** A lender that no Q7 arm reads and T4's root holds, paying the business on a line that prints invoice, payables, vendor-payment or commission wording, is released by §8.1's Q9 release as `lender_paid_for_services` under the same guard. A registered lender's credit that prints such wording (`GM FINANCIAL DES:VENDOR PMT` to a repossession agency) is D1's financing proceeds before either reading, while the same lender's `PAYABLES` there counts as `lender_paid_for_services`: releasing it would move the lender-credit exclusion (a G7 move), so it waits for the owner (§17.1).

A reversal marker still wins, because step 3 runs first. Any other credit from a listed auto lender stays financing: D1 makes it `non_revenue` / financing proceeds. S1 admits the `DEALER_FUNDING_PAYERS` lenders the ledger lacks into its vehicle-financing group, through the ledger's process. Until a lender is admitted, its credits that Q7 does not verify are held as `financing_named_payer`, whether or not its name carries a financing root; so is any row printing a dealer-funding word that Q7 did not verify (`FABRIKAM MERCHANT FUNDING DES:DEAL FUNDING`), except (audit fix batch B7, I36, §20) a wire whose purpose alone prints it from a named non-lender sender (§8.1). A dealer-funding credit is not financing proceeds, so it leaves `lender_credits` and returns to eligible deposits (an intended move).

Measured on the memo's rows: the first draft's arms (dealer wording alone) reached $4.02M, 214 rows, 11 statements. The revised rule keeps all of it: the listed-lender arms $0.37M (150 rows, 8 statements) and the credit-union arm the other $3.64M (64 rows, 4 statements of one dealer, 15 to 18 such credits in each). The corpus holds no dealer-worded credit from an unlisted, non-credit-union payer, so the tightening removes only the fabricated false positives the review built. Tryout host: $0.56M, one used-car dealer (not re-measured; the census restates it).

### 8.8 Q8: payroll and salary

`payroll_or_salary` (§8.1) is held, whoever the payer is. A payroll credit from the holder is `holder_name`. `DES:BONUS`, `DES:PAYRL`, Wells Fargo's `… DIR DEP …` to a person and an employer's `EXP REIMB` are held here, and (audit fix batch B5, I37, §20) on TD Canada Trust's statements a row whose last word is the Payments Canada payroll code `PAY` (the 200 family; `PAIE` was already read); a US row's trailing `PAY` is its own word. Audit fix batch B7 (I09, §20): a bare direct-deposit word is pay wording only with a sign of a person's pay (§8.1); a company's direct deposit to a business is its payer's credit.

### 8.9 Everything else

- A registry match that did not verify: `counted_flagged` / `platform_unconfirmed`.
- A factoring payee's credit: `counted_flagged` / `factoring_payout`. It keeps its Factoring flag. The owner deferred its Verified status (2026-09-26).
- A credit from `PAYOUT_CREDIT_ENTITIES`: `counted_flagged` / `payout_credit_entity`.
- **Lease-to-own and patient financiers (owner ruling 2026-10-02, Q8).** A credit from a lease-to-own or patient financier (`CUSTOMER_FINANCING_PAYERS`: Snap Finance, Koalafi, Acima, Progressive Leasing, Katapult, Cherry, Terrace Finance, Wisetack; each a ledger entity) is claimed as a payout entity's row is (§8.1) when all of these hold: the financier is read as the payer region; the channel is ACH, wire or other; the amount is $1 or more; the row prints no consumer-side word (OQ2's) and no legal-settlement word (`BREACH`, `LITIGAT…`, `CLASS ACTION`); and the row is not a consumer (PPD or WEB) entry to a person who is not the holder. A bare `CHERRY` is Cherry only when the whole payer region is `CHERRY` plus company or entry words; `KATAPULT ENGINEERING` and `KATAPULT PRO` are a namesake; `SNAP LOAN FUNDING` is Snap's payout only in its merchant form (§6.3 narrowing 12). It is `counted_flagged` / `customer_financing_payout`. It is never verified: an earlier rule's verification is overruled, method `customer_financing_payer`. It never counts toward a Q5 or Q6 repeat, and neither does any row that names one of them (`CUSTOMER_FINANCING_NAMES`, read without the receiver field's value). A large one-off lump sum is held as `customer_financing_lump_sum` until sourced:
  - Large: $10,000 or more, and an incoming wire, a whole multiple of $1,000, or at least half the statement's posted credits (non-revenue included, the T7 base).
  - One-off: the financier pays fewer than three payouts in the statement of at least half its amount, itself included; read over every payout at once, so a pair of lumps holds both.
  - Basis: $10,000 sits above every lease-to-own ticket ($3,500 to $7,500) and every ordinary corpus payout; a series of similar-size payouts is ordinary business and is counted.
  - Holds and debits: the claim skips the counter-debit holds as OQ2's do: for Cherry, an alternative position, that includes `payer_debited_as_lender`. Their debits keep their groups (Leases & rentals; Cherry an alternative position; a bare `CHERRY`, `WISETACK` or `TERRACE FINANCE` debit stays other). Cherry Technologies joins `PAYOUT_CREDIT_ENTITIES` and the classifier's OQ2 veto, so a `CHERRY TECHNOLOGIES` or `CHERRYPAY` merchant credit leaves D1 and its consumer-side credit keeps D1.
- A numbered company: `counted_flagged` / `numbered_company_payer` (T11).
- A named payer that Q5 or Q6 refused on a verification-only word: `counted_flagged` / `named_payer_purpose_refused`.
- A named payer on a row with no electronic-payment form (fintech exports, S51): `counted_flagged` / `named_payer_unlabelled`. It is never verified in this release. The census reports how much of it would pass Q6's test. Audit fix batch B5 (I37, §20): TD Canada Trust's trailing CPA code (`AP`, `MSP`, `BPY`, `APY`) is an electronic-payment form (§5.2), so its named payers reach Q6; the US layouts that print an originator and an entry but no ACH word (Wells Fargo, First Citizens, Found, Huntington, Truist, Mission Valley) stay here, an owner question (I37).
- A numbered company (§5.2) is no longer read from a payment reference printed before a named payer (audit fix batch B5, I59, §20).
- No payer word at all: `counted_flagged` / `no_payer_printed`.

### 8.10 Tiering order and thresholds

A Verified credit keeps its tier unless the pass overrules its verification, in this order: a factoring payer's (§8.9, `factoring_payout`), the holder's own push (§8.1, `holder_name`; audit round 2, R2-B04), a lease-to-own or patient financier's (Q8 of 2026-10-02, §8.9, `customer_financing_payout`), a listed auto lender's payables-only credit on a statement with no dealer evidence (Q9 (c') of 2026-10-02, §8.7: `lender_paid_for_services`, or `financing_named_payer` under the hidden-loan guard; R2-OW05), and a non-dealer's sale of a vehicle or heavy equipment that an invoice or customer-payment descriptor verified, on a statement with no dealer evidence (Q11 (b) of 2026-10-02, §8.1: `non_revenue` / `asset_sale_proceeds`; R2-OW06), and a builder's progress draw that an earlier rule verified (Q11 (a) of 2026-10-02, §8.1: `counted_flagged` / `construction_progress_draw`; R2-OW06 review round 1). Last, after the $1 floor, a credit into a premium trust account leaves verification (Q10 of 2026-10-02: `excluded_pending_review` / `premium_trust_account`, below; R2-OW11).

For each unverified posted credit the pass takes the first that applies:
1. `direction_conflict`
2. `insurer_payer`
3. `insurer_named_payer`
4. `possible_return`
5. `financing_named_payer`
6. `payer_debited_as_lender`
7. `holder_name`
8. `payroll_or_salary`
9. `personal_income`
10. `non_sale_purpose`
11. `payer_also_debited`; then (audit fix batch B4) a payroll provider's tax-service credit as `non_sale_purpose`; then, past the holds (and audit fix batch B2's named sender after an own-account designation, held as `transfer_account_designation`) and before the wires, an insurer paid for the business's work (`insurer_paid_for_services`, the underwriter's Q2 of 2026-10-02, §8.1: the release's method, which only holds 4 to 11 and that designation hold precede; inserted here rather than renumbered, as Q8's and Q11's tiers were, so step 26 keeps its number), a factoring payer's payout (`factoring_payout`, A3-H: `FACTORING_PAYOUT_PAYERS`) and a lease-to-own or patient financier's payout (`customer_financing_payout`, Q8 of 2026-10-02, §8.9); then a builder's progress draw (`construction_progress_draw`, Q11 (a) of 2026-10-02, §8.1: any channel but Zelle; a bare transfer's and an account designation's holds and Q4's round-sum repeat still win)
12. wires (§8.5: `wire_no_sender`, `wire_named_sender` or `named_payer_purpose_refused`)
13. `transfer_no_counterparty` (before the check and branch tiers, so `TELLER TRANSFER` is held)
14. `transfer_account_designation`
15. `check_deposit`
16. cash, branch, ATM (`no_payer_printed`)
17. person-to-person and named transfers (`p2p_round_repeat`, or `p2p`)
18. `platform_unconfirmed`
19. `factoring_payout` (a credit the classifier reads as factoring)
20. `payout_credit_entity`
21. `numbered_company_payer`
22. `named_payer_purpose_refused`
23. `named_payer_one_off`
24. `named_payer_unlabelled`
25. `no_payer_printed` (audit fix batch B10: `payer_text_not_read` on a row the parser marked as read only by its label, here only; B10 review round 1: never at 16, where the cash, branch, teller or ATM label says the statement printed no payer; audit round 2, R2-B07: `unread_run_names_financing`, held, where that row's unread payer text prints a lender's or a lending bank's block, §8.2)

The Q9 relabel (owner ruling 2026-10-02, the underwriter's Q9; §8.1; R2-OW09), last, after step 25's unread branch: a credit the financing-root release lifted (`finance_named_customer`, `lessor_rent` or `lender_paid_for_services`) that steps 12 to 25 count takes the release's reason in place of theirs. Held reasons, `payer_text_not_read` and the kept reasons (`numbered_company_payer`, `factoring_payout`, `payout_credit_entity`, `platform_unconfirmed`, `customer_financing_payout`, `construction_progress_draw`, `insurer_paid_for_services`, `lender_paid_for_services`) win. Such a credit is never verified and never counts toward a Q5 or Q6 repeat; the asset-sale override and the Zelle step (26) still read it after.

Each row's tier taken (owner ruling 2026-10-02, Q11 (b); §8.1): a row the steps above count, or one IAA's insurer-name hold alone holds (no later hold would name it; R2-OW06 review round 1), that the asset-sale reading reads on a statement with no dealer evidence becomes `non_revenue` / `asset_sale_proceeds`; every other hold keeps it held.

After the tiers (owner ruling 2026-10-02, Q8; §8.9), a one-off lump sum among the `customer_financing_payout` rows, the verified ones the pass overruled included, is held as `customer_financing_lump_sum`; then the Zelle policy (26) and the $1 floor.

26. Then, in the stored reading, after every step above and before the $1 floor, the Zelle policy (owner ruling 2026-10-02, the underwriter's Q3; §8.4): a Zelle deposit the steps above verified, counted or held is `non_revenue` / `zelle_excluded`, its reading kept; the floor and every later step skip it (it is `non_revenue`). The step runs in the stored (No) reading; the counted reading skips it and the two lifted carve-outs (the owner's amendment of 2026-10-06 to the underwriter's Q3, R2-OW17; §8.1, §8.4), and its later steps read the counted tiers.

Then, after the $1 floor, the premium-trust hold (owner ruling 2026-10-02, the underwriter's Q10, "Hold every deposit into an account titled "premium trust""; §2.1, §9.1; R2-OW11). On a statement whose account title reads PREMIUM TRUST (`premium_trust_title` over `Statement.account_title`, `account_name`, `holder_name`: the title at the field's end, the title followed by an account word, or the title and an account or product word followed by a separator), every verified or counted posted credit is held as `premium_trust_account`. A verified one leaves verification (method `premium_trust_account`, rule `premium_trust_account_title`, its reason naming the rule it overruled). A held one keeps its first hold, and a non-revenue one stays non-revenue. In detail:
- The rule reads the statement's own fields in order: the bank's designation (`account_title`, R2-OW10) in any of the three forms (never the words anywhere: a trade name the holder reader dropped after a legal form, `PREMIUM TRUST ROOFING`, is no title); then the account name, then the holder's name, each in the end form, in the account-word form only when the field does not end in a legal form (`PREMIUM TRUST ACCOUNT LLC` is a company), and in the separator form even when it does (`PREMIUM TRUST ACCOUNT - NORTHWIND INSURANCE AGENCY LLC`). The words are whole (`PREM`, `PREMIUM` or `PREMIUMS`, then `TRUST` or `TRST`, a dot after either allowed; never `TRUSTEE` or `SUPREMIUM`); the separator form needs an account or product word (never `FUND`, `FUNDS` or a bare title before a dash). It never reads a row, so a payer that prints the words makes no title. Recorded false negatives, the safe direction and absent from the corpus: `PREM. TR. ACCT.`, a nickname with no account word before a separator.
- The hold follows every step: the Q5, Q6 and Q7 verifications, the demotions, the insurer-for-work release (the underwriter's Q2: a carrier's commission it counts on a trust account is held here), the customer-financing lump sum, the Zelle step and the floor. Q5's and Q6's repeat counts are unchanged. A cash, branch, ATM or bare deposit into a premium trust account is held for the title, not for being cash.
- The agency's operating, producer-payable, wire and Lloyd's-titled accounts, a credit union's checking beside an empty premium-trust share, a `PREMIUM BUSINESS` product, an IOLTA or escrow account and a family trust read as before.

Holds 2 to 11 are §8.1's; the owner's own holds (Q2, Q4, Q5, Q8 and the holder) are among them or in tiers 12 to 17.

| Threshold | Value | Where |
|---|---|---|
| Repeats | 2 or more credits, same payer, one statement | §5.2, Q5, Q6 |
| Round sum | at least $100, a whole multiple of $100 | §5.2, Q4 |
| Round-sum repeat | 2 or more round sums from one sender, rails and named transfers alike | §8.4 |
| Credit-union dealer funding | 2 or more `VHCL PURCH` credits from credit unions in the statement | §8.7 |
| Operating recurrence | 3 or more credits, or 2 on a business account (a legal-form holder counts) | §7.0 |
| Micro-deposit floor | under $1 never verifies and never counts | §7.0, §7.8, §7.10 |
| NET SETTLE from an unregistered originator | 3 or more credits | §7.1 |
| Auction refund window | 14 days, equal amount, one debit each | §7.8 |
| Package gate | held credits at least 10% of all posted credits, non-revenue included, in integer cents (`REVENUE_REVIEW_HELD_SHARE`) | T7 |
| Customer-financing lump sum | $10,000 or more and a wire, a whole $1,000 multiple or at least 50% of the statement's posted credits (`CUSTOMER_FINANCING_LUMP_FLOOR`, `CUSTOMER_FINANCING_LUMP_ROUND`, `CUSTOMER_FINANCING_LUMP_SHARE`) | §8.9 |
| Customer-financing series | 3 or more payouts from one financier in the statement, each at least 50% of the row's amount (not one-off) (`CUSTOMER_FINANCING_SERIES_MIN`, `CUSTOMER_FINANCING_SERIES_SHARE`) | §8.9 |
| Insurer for work | 3 or more eligible credits from one insurer key within an inclusive 31-day span (date[i+2] - date[i] ≤ 30 days; the span slides across a calendar month's edge; an undated credit counts as inside), one statement; a loose trade word needs 2 or more eligible insurer credits in the statement (`INSURER_FOR_WORK_MIN_CREDITS`, `INSURER_FOR_WORK_WINDOW_DAYS`, `INSURER_FOR_WORK_LOOSE_MIN_CREDITS`; the Q2 card's checker measured 3 groups, 9 rows, $19,110.19 on the first card's rows that no calendar month holds, not re-measured under the revision) | §8.1 |

Each threshold is one named integer constant ($1 as `1`, $100 as `100`, 10% as `10`). The classification thresholds live in `analysis/transaction_classifier.py`. The gate's `REVENUE_REVIEW_HELD_SHARE` lives in `analysis/revenue.py`, which the metrics and the webapp both import.

## 9. The data contract

### 9.1 Per account (`report_to_dict` / `rebuild_serialized_revenue_views`)

- **Rows:** every `statement.transactions[].classification` carries `revenue_tier`, `revenue_initial_tier`, `revenue_tier_reason` and the flags of §5.4 (5.6). Audit fix batch B9 (I13, §20): and the statement's `holder_name`, beside `account_name`. The underwriter's Q1 (2026-10-02; R2-OW12, §20): and `revenue_funding_series` (§5.4), a list of objects, empty on every row but a held `wire_no_sender` credit; it rides in every copy of the record (the classifications, the evidence lists, the package ledger, the evidence JSON cells of the exports and the JSON download), and the posted-credit export table gains no column. The underwriter's Q5 (2026-10-02; R2-OW13, §20): and, right after `settlement_reversal`, `returned_funder_payment_by` (on a confirmed funder's payment returned unpaid, the return credit's location) and `returns_funder_payment` (on that credit, the payment's location), `null` on every other row.
- **Transactions:** audit fix batch B10 (I05, I60, §20): `statement.transactions[].payer_text_unread` is `true` on a credit whose parser published only its own label because it could not read the payer the statement printed (§8.2); the key is written only where it is set, so no other transaction gains a key, and it is not part of the extraction response schema (the extractor is told nothing new). Audit round 2, R2-B07 (R07, §20): `statement.transactions[].unread_payer_text` is, on a credit the counted core-processor template marked at a welded flush, that flush's joined text (several rows' payer blocks, never proven this row's, so never its description); written only where it is set and kept out of the extraction response schema, as `payer_text_unread` is.
- **Statement:** audit fix batch B9 (I13, §20): `statement.holder_name` is the holder's name the parser read from the header or the mailing block (Chase, First Citizens, TD Bank, Truist, PNC, Navy Federal, TD Canada Trust; audit round 2, R2-B05: R04 part 2, page 1's mailing address of Bank of America, Wells Fargo, U.S. Bank, RBC and Banque Royale, Scotiabank, Bluevine, Huntington, Capital One, CIBC, Square, Mission Valley, BMO's US activity layout, Santander, Citibank and TD Canada Trust's French issue), never the parser's own product (audit fix batch B9 review round 1: PNC's product printed in capitals on its summary title), or `null`; `statement.account_name` keeps the printed product, nickname or name (Chase no longer publishes its summary grid header there). Owner ruling 2026-10-02 (the underwriter's Q10, its parser half), audit round 2, R2-OW10 (§20): `statement.account_title` is the title the bank prints after the holder's name (a premium trust, an operating, a wire or a producer-payable account), read from the holder reader's own anchor: the words that reader drops after the name it publishes, never other text, and none where it reads no name. It is serialized only where it is set, so no other statement gains a key, and it is not part of the extraction response schema (the extractor is told nothing new). It is provenance for the revenue rule (R2-OW11); in R2-OW10 no hold, holder test, tier or figure reads it, and it never enters the holder's names. Owner ruling 2026-10-02 (the underwriter's Q10), R2-OW11 (§8.10, §20): its one reader is the premium-trust rule (`premium_trust_title`, with the account name and the holder's name), which holds a premium trust account's credits that would count; the holder's names still never read it.
- **Metrics:** unchanged keys keep their meaning. New keys:
  - `true_revenue_total`, `true_revenue_count`;
  - `counted_flagged_total`, `counted_flagged_count`;
  - `excluded_pending_review_total`, `excluded_pending_review_count`;
  - `counted_flagged_by_reason` and `excluded_pending_review_by_reason`, each `{reason: {"count": int, "total": float}}`;
  - audit round 2, R2-OW03 (owner ruling 2026-10-02, §20): `non_revenue_by_reason`, the same shape over the `non_revenue` rows that carry a code `REVENUE_TIER_REASONS` files under `non_revenue` (§5.3: `zelle_excluded`, `government_no_purpose`), a dict of its own, never a slot of the counted or held maps (a reviewer's rejection keeps its counted or held code and is not listed). `compute_metrics` and the rebuild compute it by one rule; it is one of `TIER_METRIC_KEYS`, so a payload analysed before 5.6 has it `None` (§12);
  - `revenue_review_items`, the held count;
  - audit fix batch B9 (I13, §20): `holder_unscreened`, true when no holder's name is known for the statement (no parser `holder_name`, no account name that names a holder, no holder name in the statement's own receiver fields), so the holds that read the holder's name cannot see the holder's own money; the True card and the exports show it in audit batch B11;
  - audit fix batch B10 (I05, §20): `payer_text_unread`, true when more than 30% (`PAYER_TEXT_UNREAD_SHARE`) of the statement's posted credit rows, duplicates aside, carry the parser's 'payer text not read' mark, so its True rests on credits whose payer nobody read; and `payer_text_unread_count`, how many posted credits carry it. A statement integrity fact for the True card (audit batch B11);
  - owner ruling 2026-10-02 (the underwriter's Q10), R2-OW11 (§8.10, §20): `premium_trust_account`, true when the statement's printed title reads PREMIUM TRUST (`premium_trust_title` over its account title, account name and holder name), so pass 7 holds every credit a rule verified or counted. A statement fact for the True card and the package (§9.2, §10.1); no figure reads it.

  - owner ruling 2026-10-02 (the underwriter's Q5), R2-OW13 (§11, §20): `returned_funder_payment_total`, `returned_funder_payment_count` and `returned_funder_payment_evidence`, the debits that carry `returned_funder_payment_by`. `lender_debits` and `lender_debit_count` stay the paid rows (`contributes_to_lender_totals`, paid to lenders); `withholding_numerator` is every row that `contributes_to_withholding_rate` (paid plus returned, equal to `lender_debits + returned_funder_payment_total` to the cent; it was `lender_debits`); `withholding_formula` reads "abs(paid lender debits + returned funder payments) / withholding basis * 100" and `potential_withholding_formula` "abs(potential_lender_debit_total) / withholding basis * 100"; a note names the returned payments in the statement's currency. `lenders_detected` counts a funder whose every payment bounced (it stays in the lender count).

  - owner ruling 2026-10-02 (the underwriter's Q6), R2-OW15 (§6.2's package passes, §20): the served copy (`apply_revenue_view`'s `_served_account`; never stored) adds, each only where its count is above 0, `unmatched_deposit_return_count`, `unmatched_deposit_return_total` and `unmatched_deposit_return_locations` (the debits that undo a deposit, `_deposit_return_debit`, that no credit of the statement pairs) and `processor_chargeback_count`, `processor_chargeback_total` and `processor_chargeback_locations` (a processor's chargebacks and adjustments, `processor_chargeback_debit`), each total the debits' magnitude (`debit_side_flags`, `debit_flag_metrics`). They are flags, never deducted: no figure, tier, gate or lender reading reads them, and a statement without one is served as before.

  `true_revenue` is repointed to `true_revenue_total` (T9). `revenue_review_required` means the gate of T7. `revenue_reconciles` checks the four-tier identity (§5.1). Audit fix batch B11 (I31, §20): the identity is published under its own name, `revenue_tiers_sum_to_posted`, and `revenue_reconciles` stays as its deprecated alias; neither is a reconciliation against the bank's figures (`reconciliation.ok`), and the dashboard no longer reads either as one.
- **Detection:** `true_revenue_evidence` is repointed to verified plus counted. `counted_flagged_evidence` and `excluded_pending_review_evidence` are new. `manual_review` holds the rows whose `revenue_review_required` is set (held rows) plus today's `review_required` rows. Owner ruling 2026-10-02 (the underwriter's Q5), R2-OW13 (§20): `returned_funder_payments` lists one item per returned funder payment (`funder`, `amount`, `debit_date`, `debit_location`, `credit_date`, `credit_location`, `credit_description`, the return as the bank printed it); each `known_funders` entry adds `returned_payment_count` and `returned_payment_total` (its `debit_count` and `total_debited` stay paid; its `transactions` and `evidence` hold the returned rows too), and a funder whose every payment bounced is listed with `debit_count` 0; `lender_evidence` stays the paid rows.
- **Withholding:** `WITHHOLDING_DENOMINATOR_MODES` gains `true_revenue` (§11).
- **The two Zelle readings (the owner's amendment of 2026-10-06 to the underwriter's Q3; R2-OW17, §8.4, §20):**
  - *Stored.* The payload is the stored (No) reading, built exactly as before. An account whose counted (Yes) reading differs carries, after the rebuild, the account key `zelle_counted_reading`: the lean edits that turn the stored account into the counted one (`analysis/zelle_view.py` `reading_edits`). Each edit is `[path, value]` (set) or `[path]` (delete), a path being the dict keys and list indexes into the account; dicts are compared key by key, lists of equal length element by element, anything else is replaced whole. The list is lean: it drops every edit under a path the revenue rebuild writes (`REBUILT_KEYS`: the revenue metrics and their evidence lists, the recomputed withholding figures, the detection evidence and `manual_review`, the `classifications` view and each statement row's contribution flags), because every reading is rebuilt after its edits are applied; and it is exact either way (when the rebuild of the applied lean list is not the counted payload, the full list is stored). The key is written only when the edits are non-empty, so a statement with no Zelle row publishes today's payload byte for byte; `account_content_digest` includes it. `Report.zelle_counted` holds the counted reading on the object (never serialized as itself).
  - *Served* (`apply_zelle_view`, the first step of every served copy; display keys, never stored). The setting's reading is materialised (`reading`: the edits applied and the account rebuilt; an account whose edits cannot be applied is served as stored). An account's **Zelle rows** are its stored reading's posted, non-duplicate credits of method `zelle_deposit_excluded` (the excluded ones and those a reviewer has confirmed since); an account with none is a **legacy** account when a counted, held or verified credit reads the Zelle rail (analysed before the policy, its Zelle natively counted; those credits are its Zelle rows). `metrics.zelle_deposits` = `{counted_as_true_revenue, setting_applied, count, total, by_tier: {tier: {count, total}}}` over the Zelle rows in the reading served (`zelle_deposit_figures`, money rounded as the non-revenue breakdown's); its parts are **in True** (verified plus counted), **held** and **out** (non-revenue). It is served under Yes on every account with Zelle rows, and under No only where today's output would misstate where the Zelle money sits (a Zelle row whose served tier is not `non_revenue`, or `setting_applied` false), so a fresh No analysis is today's payload exactly. `counted_as_true_revenue` is the reading served (a legacy account is served as stored, so true there); `setting_applied` is false under Yes on an account with Zelle rows and no usable edits (analysed between R2-OW02 and R2-OW17), and under No on a legacy account. Under Yes each Zelle row's served transaction carries `zelle_deposit: true` (the owner's "flagged 'Zelle'"), kept in the downloads.

- **Lender payment changes (the owner's request of 2026-10-06; R2-OW18, §20):**
  - *Detection.* `detection.lender_payment_changes`, after `returned_funder_payments`: one item per signal (`kind` `decrease`, `increase`, `cadence_change`, `pause`, `new_stream` or `stop`; `analysis/lender_payment_changes.py`), ordered confirmed first, then by lender, series, position and date. Every item: `lender` (the canonical entity), `lender_label` (a potential payee's label, else the entity), `lender_state` (`confirmed`, `potential`), `position`, `positions`, `scope` (`statement`). A change: `lender_label_after`, `cadence_before`, `cadence_after`, `amount_before`, `amount_after`, `change_percent` (an integer, on the compared amounts), `cadence_changed`, `schedule_confirmed` (false on a possible change), `weekly_equivalent_before` and `_after` (with `cadence_changed`), `payments_before`, `payments_after`, `last_before_date`, `first_after_date`, `last_after_date`, `restart`, `pause_business_days`, `back_to_earlier`, `reverted`, `reverted_date`, `via` (the unreported levels between the reference and the new level, each with `amount`, `cadence` and `change_percent`, the step into it), `last_step_percent` (with `via`: the step from the last of them to the new level; R2-OW18 review round 1) and `after_funding`. A pause: `cadence`, `last_payment_amount`, `last_before_date`, `first_after_date`, `first_after_kind` (what ended it: `payment`, the regime's next payment; `attempt`, a bounced or reversed debit; `other_amount`, a payment of the series at another amount), `resumed_date` (the regime's next payment; R2-OW18 review round 1), `pause_business_days`, `grace_business_days`. A new stream: `cadence_after`, `amount_after`, `first_after_date`, `payments_after`, `alongside`, `weekly_total_before`, `weekly_total_after`, `change_percent`. A stop: `cadence`, `last_payment_date`, `last_payment_amount`, `payments`, `last_presence_date`, `quiet_business_days`, `grace_business_days`, `coverage_end`, `coverage_end_source` (`period_end`, or `last_transaction` where none is printed), `stop_confirmed` (never true inside one statement) and its notes `other_debits_after`, `payoff`, `continues_as`, `other_stream_continues`, `last_attempt_returned`, `debt_relief_after`, `new_lender_after`. And `locations` (source locations). A nested note is absent when not set; no key is named `account`. `detect()` computes it in each Zelle reading (R2-OW17), so the reading served carries its own; a review decision leaves it as it is. An empty list means checked, no change.
  - *Rows.* Every record gains `potential_payee_key` after `potential_payee_label`: on every `potential_lender` row, named or not, an amount-free digest of its payee key (the entity, D6's payee words and the masked recipient; the first 16 hex characters of their SHA-256), so no payee word is published; None elsewhere. Only the module reads it.

### 9.2 Package (`_package_analysis`)

- **Each document row** gains:
  - `true_revenue_total`, `true_revenue_count`, `counted_flagged_total`, `counted_flagged_count`, `excluded_pending_review_total`, `excluded_pending_review_count` and the two by-reason dicts;
  - `revenue_established`. It is today's `verified_revenue_established` condition (`webapp/app.py:1367-1376`) and every posted credit carries a 5.6 tier. `verified_revenue_established` stays, with the old condition, for the verified figure.
- **Totals:**
  - the same keys, summed over the members;
  - `true_revenue_total`, `counted_flagged_total`, `excluded_pending_review_total` and their counts are `None` when any completed member's `revenue_established` is false, and `verified_revenue_total` is `None` when any completed member's `verified_revenue_established` is false (§10.4);
  - `revenue_unestablished_documents` lists those members' ids;
  - `revenue_review_items` is the sum of the members' held counts;
  - `revenue_review_required` is the gate of T7, applied to each member.
- **Evidence:** the package's revenue evidence stays per state, and each evidence record carries its tier fields. The package's own `true_revenue_evidence`, at the top level (`webapp/app.py:2155`) and inside `detection` (`:2167`), is repointed with the per-account one: the members' verified plus counted evidence, not `package_revenue_evidence["verified_revenue"]`. `counted_flagged_evidence` and `excluded_pending_review_evidence` join both places.
- **Fallbacks:** `_package_analysis` reads `metrics["true_revenue"]` twice as a fallback today: for a member's verified total when its rows are not authoritative (`:1441-1447`, after `verified_revenue_total` and `confirmed_true_revenue_total`), and for the withholding denominator when `withholding_denominator` is missing (`:1471-1474`). After the repoint that key is True revenue, so both fallbacks are dropped: the verified total falls back to `verified_revenue_total`, then `confirmed_true_revenue_total`, then `None` (the member's verified figure is not established); the denominator falls back to the legacy eligible deposits.
- **Currency:** the new money keys join `_CROSS_CURRENCY_TOTAL_KEYS` and the test's `EXPECTED_REFUSED_TOTALS`, the counts join `UNIT_FREE_TOTALS`, and a refused package sets every `total` inside the by-reason dicts to `None`.
- **Audit fix batch B11 (§20):**
  - *Duplicates (I06, MCA standard §4.6(3)).* Before any member is expanded, a job that repeats a kept job's id, content hash, or (account by account) statement identity is left out of every figure: an account's content digest when its ledger prints a transaction, or its statement key when every part is printed (bank, account last four, period start and end, opening and closing balance), never between two printed full numbers that conflict (audit round 2, R2-B14 below). Which copy is kept is R2-B14's rank below. It is listed in `documents` after the members (`is_duplicate`, `duplicate_of`, `duplicate_reason` `same_content` or `same_statement`, `duplicate_kept_because`, no figure), its group in `duplicates`; a job listed twice is listed once. An account of a kept document that another kept job published is excluded (`excluded_accounts`, reason `duplicate_statement`, `duplicate_accounts` in the totals); the sibling accounts of one document are never compared. Any duplicate sends the package to review. The ids of `?ids=` and `POST /package` are de-duplicated.
  - *Months and averages (I07, I33).* `months` is the number of distinct calendar months the counted statements stand for (the Monthly Statements' rule: the month holding most of a period's days, the earlier on a tie; a statement printing no period is its own month), no longer the member count; `statement_periods` is published beside it when the two differ. `avg_monthly_true_revenue`, `avg_monthly_verified_revenue` and `avg_monthly_non_revenue` are the package totals over `months` (so the per-calendar-month sum across accounts, averaged), `None` where True is N/A, and refused with the other per-period averages (one document's accounts, a mixed or undeclared currency).
  - *Reconciliation (I31).* The totals and each document row carry `revenue_tiers_sum_to_posted` beside `revenue_reconciles`; `unreconciled_documents` lists the counted members whose `reconciliation.ok` is not true. The decision no longer reads the identity.
  - *Integrity facts (B9's I13, B10's I05).* Each document row carries `holder_unscreened` and `payer_text_unread`; the totals list the members (`holder_unscreened_documents`, `payer_text_unread_documents`).
  - *Evidence (I32).* Each revenue evidence record carries `source_currency` and `source_account` (`None` for a statement of one account).
- **Audit round 2, R2-B14 (§20):**
  - *Which copy of a repeated statement is kept (R16).* The listed jobs claim their ids, hashes and identities in the order of a rank, then of their listed place: a job that is done and publishes an account first, then one whose served copy is current (no account with `revenue_established` false, no record without or before `CLASSIFICATION_VERSION`), then one whose posted credits carry an analyst's decision (`revenue_review_status` confirmed or rejected). So a failed, queued, processing or interrupted copy, a copy analysed under older rules or a copy without the decisions recorded on another never takes a better copy's place; copies alike keep the one listed first. `documents` and `duplicates` keep the listed order (a group lists the kept job first, its hash the group's); each left-out row's `duplicate_kept_because` is the first rank key the kept copy wins on (`has_analysis`, `current_rules`, `has_review_decisions`), else `listed_first`. A left-out failed copy is not counted failed.
  - *Two accounts are never one statement by the last four alone (R46).* The statement key matches only between accounts whose printed numbers do not conflict: the digits at the end of each number (blanks, `-`, `.` and `/` removed) conflict when both print more than four and the shorter's are not the end of the longer's. A masked or four-digit print still matches a full one, and a content digest (which covers the number) matches as before.
  - *A shorter printout of days another statement covers (R14).* After the exact repeats, the statements the package counts are grouped by their bank (casefolded) and their printed number's last four (never two whose full numbers conflict, never two accounts of one document); a statement's period is its printed one, or else its first and last posted row's day. A statement is left out (its `duplicate_of` the statement left in the package that shares the most of its days) when its period lies inside the union of the other statements' periods of its account, it prints a posted row, and every posted row of it, credit or debit, is one of theirs as a multiset on the day and the signed cents. The statements of more than a month (31 days) are tested first, the longest first: a quarterly printout or a multi-month export whose rows the monthly statements print is left out (`duplicate_reason` `superseded_long_printout`) and the monthly statements, each its own calendar month, stay. Then the rest, the shortest first: a month-to-date or interim printout beside the full month, the shorter of two month-to-date printouts or a short custom range the full months print is left out (`superseded_interim`), and a full month is never left out for partial printouts of it (of two periods alike, the later listed is tested first; review round 1). An account of a document whose other accounts stay is excluded alone (`excluded_accounts`, the same reason). Like a repeat, it sends the package to review. Any other overlap of two statements of one account is never netted: when the two share a credit in the days both cover (a multiset on the day, the cents and the description, casefolded, its blanks collapsed), `overlapping_statements` lists the pair (`job`, the one listed later, `other`, `shared_credit_count`, `shared_credit_total`, `currency`, the account's, null when the two declare different ones, and `account` / `other_account` for an account of a document) and the package goes to review; boundary days that share no credit say nothing. A package without such a statement is unchanged.
- **Audit round 2, R2-B15 (§20):**
  - *Months by the days the statements cover (R13).* `months` is the larger of B11's distinct calendar months (above, unchanged, as are the Month/Year labels) and a floor: the days each account's counted statements cover (`_covered_days`: a printed period's days, first and last included, none when a day does not read or the end is before the start, at most 400), as whole months of 30.4375 days, half up, the largest account's. An account is its bank, casefolded and its blanks collapsed, and the last four digits of its printed number; a member printing neither is its own. So three statements of a 16th-to-15th cycle across February, of a business-day cycle slipping around the 15th, or of a cycle whose periods share their closing day read 3 months (B11's rule read 2), and a statement of 59 days reads 2 (it read 1); calendar months never read fewer than before.
  - *Accounts left out for another reason than a repeat (R15).* Membership and every figure are unchanged (Q1, Q2, Q5 of 2026-08-30; the main-account ruling of 2026-09-23). Each `excluded_accounts` entry names its statement's `filename`. When an entry is not a repeat (`is_duplicate`): a statement whose main account is held or idle, an account that did not validate on its own, every account of a document whose transfers could not be paired or that left a section out without proof, the totals publish `completeness` `partial` (Q1: the package surfaces partial completeness) and `excluded_account_count`, and the package goes to review, as the same account uploaded alone does. `sibling_account_omission_detected` stays Q10's (a ratified omission stays partial and approved).
  - *No statement analysed, and jobs still on their way (R54).* With no completed member (every job failed, was interrupted or is still queued or processing, or every account was left out), the True, Verified, Counted and Held totals, their counts, aliases (`true_revenue`, `confirmed_true_revenue`, `confirmed_true_revenue_total`) and by-reason dicts are `None`, so the per-month True and Verified are too, `revenue_tiers_sum_to_posted` and `revenue_reconciles` are false and `true_revenue_evidence` is `None`; `total_credits`, the gross averages, non-revenue and the currency layer's `no_analyzed_documents` keep their structural zeros. A job still queued or processing is counted under `pending` (published only when there is one), never `failed`, and sends the package to review; an error, an interrupted run and a job done without an analysis stay `failed`. With a completed member §10.4 holds as before.
  - *`monthly_lender_debits` (R55)* is the confirmed lender debits per calendar month, `lender_debits / months`, refused with the other per-period figures (one document's accounts, a mixed or undeclared currency); it was the package's total under a monthly name. A statement's own `monthly_lender_debits` (`analysis/metrics.py`) is unchanged.
- **Audit round 2, R2-OW03 (owner ruling 2026-10-02, the underwriter's Q3; §20):** each document row and the totals carry `non_revenue_by_reason` (§9.1), the row's from its own rows (the rows `non_revenue_total` reads, its internal-transfer pairs left out) or, without classification records, from its stored metrics, and the totals' summed over the kept members only (never a repeat, a superseded printout or an account left out). It is never nulled where revenue is not established (§10.4: Non-revenue stays), nor by R54's no-statement-analysed block (it is then empty); under a currency refusal each total inside it is `None` and the counts stay, as for the other by-reason dicts, while each document row keeps its own denominated figures.
- **Owner ruling 2026-10-02 (the underwriter's Q10), R2-OW11 (§20):** each document row carries `premium_trust_account` (its metrics' fact), and the totals list the counted members that are premium trust accounts (`premium_trust_documents`, sorted, beside `holder_unscreened_documents` and `payer_text_unread_documents`).
- **Owner ruling 2026-10-02 (the underwriter's Q5), R2-OW13 (§11, §20):** the paid figure (`lender_debits`, `lender_debit_count`) reads `contributes_to_lender_totals` (it read `contributes_to_withholding_rate`, equal until the ruling). Each document row's `withholding_numerator` is its own, paid plus returned (it was its `lender_debits`; a member without classification records reads its stored `withholding_numerator`, else its `lender_debits`), and the totals' sums the members' (it was the package's paid figure). Document rows and totals carry `returned_funder_payment_total` (refused across currencies, `_CROSS_CURRENCY_TOTAL_KEYS`) and `returned_funder_payment_count` (a count, kept); each funder rollup sums `returned_payment_count` and `returned_payment_total` (refused across currencies, `_CROSS_CURRENCY_ROLLUP_KEYS`) and publishes a `debit_count` of 0 for a funder whose every payment bounced. The package lists `returned_funder_payments` over its kept members, each item naming its `source_job`, `source_document`, `source_currency` (and `source_account` for an account of a document), its money its statement's own. `lender_evidence` keeps the withholding flag, so the returned rows are listed and marked. The `withholding_formula` and `potential_withholding_formula` strings are §9.1's.
- **Owner ruling 2026-10-02 (the underwriter's Q6), R2-OW15 (§6.2's package passes, §11, §20):**
  - *The overlay.* Right after a member's rows are read and before R-d's positions are left out, the member loop replaces each row the passes matched or annotated with a new copy whose classification carries their fields (the displayed copy and the stored job are never touched), so every reader after it sees them: the tiers and their reasons, the revenue rows and evidence, the member's gate, the ledger and the document row. A deposit pass 1 takes out of True reads `revenue_classification` and `revenue_tier` `non_revenue`, `revenue_tier_reason` none, method `matched_reversal_pair`, rule `returned_deposit_cross_statement`, `revenue_review_required` false and the contribution flags of `non_revenue`, and `package_match` `{kind: "returned_deposit", moved: true, debit: {job, filename, account_index, source_location, date, amount, bank, last4}, gap_days, tier_before, reason_before}`; its initial state, review status and pass-4 link are kept. Its return's row carries `package_match` `{kind: "returned_deposit", credit: {...}}`, a display note only.

- **Owner ruling 2026-10-02 (the underwriter's Q4), R2-OW16 (§6.2's package passes, §11, §20):**
  - *The overlay.* A deposit pass 2 holds reads `revenue_tier` `excluded_pending_review`, `revenue_tier_reason` `own_account_transfer_matched`, `revenue_classification` `unverified_deposit` (unchanged), `revenue_review_required` true and the contribution flags of a held `unverified_deposit`, and `package_match` `{kind: "own_account_transfer", moved: true, debit: {job, filename, account_index, source_location, date, amount, bank, last4}, gap_days, tier_before, reason_before}`; its initial state and pending status are kept, so the package ledger offers Confirm Revenue and Mark Non-Revenue.
