  - *Lists:* `package_matches` gains an `own_account_transfer` entry for each pair (`moved` true for a held deposit, false for an annotated one), in the canonical order after pass 1's.
  - *Document rows:* `package_match_unchecked` may read `no_account_number` (a member that prints fewer than four digits of its account number, in a package of two members or more), and `package_match_unchecked_count` counts it; `package_match_count` counts the pair's rows on each member.

- **The owner's amendment of 2026-10-06 to the underwriter's Q3, R2-OW17 (§9.1, §20):** the members are the displayed copies in the setting's Zelle reading, so the member rows, tier totals, by-reason figures, gate, review items, evidence, monthly rows and each member's withholding denominator follow it. The totals gain `zelle_deposits` (§9.1's shape), the kept members' figures summed part by part, present when a kept member carries them; under No a kept member without them contributes its `non_revenue_by_reason.zelle_excluded` as its out part, so the figure covers every member; `counted_as_true_revenue` is the setting and `setting_applied` is false when any member's is. Each document row carries its member's `zelle_deposits` where the member does. A currency refusal nulls the totals' `total` and every `by_tier` total and keeps every count (a dedicated pass; the refused-field list is unchanged). The package's flattened `transactions` keep each row's `zelle_deposit` tag.

- **The owner's request of 2026-10-06 (lender payment changes), R2-OW18 (§20):** `lender_payment_changes`, a list wherever at least one member was assessed (absent when none was): each lender payment series read across the consecutive statements of one account (`_package_lender_payment_changes`, after the member loop: the kept members' displayed copies with R2-OW15's overlay, in canonical order, each joining the first chain whose last member is `_same_account` and ends `LENDER_CHAIN_OVERLAP_DAYS = 5` days after to `PACKAGE_CONSECUTIVE_DAYS` before it starts; the module's overlap de-duplication; scope `package`). Each item carries `source_job`, `source_document`, `source_account` (a statement of several accounts), `source_currency` and `source_period_end` (the statement of the first payment at the new amount, the resuming presence or the last presence); a change also `from_job`, `from_document`, `from_account` (the last old payment's statement), `to_job`, `to_document`, `to_account` (the new regime's second payment's) and `cross_statement`. A stop is `stop_confirmed` only when later statements of its chain cover 80% of a cycle; one whose series pays or is attempted later in a chain of another account of the package carries `continues_in_other_account` and is never confirmed. `lender_payment_changes_unchecked` lists the members not checked across statements, only where there is one: `not_ready`, `analysed_before_check`, `no_currency`, `no_period`, `no_account_number` (fewer than four digits and no balance chain). Never summed: no totals, document-row or rollup key, and the currency refusal leaves each item in its own unit.

So an analysis saved at 5.6 gets the re-analyze notice, and its Re-analyze misses the stage-32 cache entry (`_CacheOnly` passes `get_analysis` through) and recomputes the analysis from the cached reading; with 5.7 alone the cached 5.6 entry would come back and the notice would survive its own button. Each `ANALYSIS_STAGE_VERSION` bump makes a re-upload, and a re-analysis, recompute the analysis from the cached reading and keeps OCR cached. Only a `CLASSIFICATION_VERSION` move sets `analysis_rules_outdated` on older saved analyses (lender spec D12): a stage-only bump (B9 to B11, R2-B04 to R2-B07 above) sets no notice, and 5.7 sets it on every analysis saved at 5.6 or earlier (audit round 2, R2-B16: R56).

### 10.2 Monthly Statements

The Settings basis keeps its three views (both, total, true), which are stored in the browser only. A single-basis view keeps the CRM's own headers, as today.
- **The True view:** "Monthly Deposits ($)" (True revenue), "Deposits Per Month" (verified plus counted rows) and, new, "Verified ($)".
- **The Both view:** "Total Deposits ($)", "Total Deposits Per Month", "True Deposits ($)" (True revenue), "True Deposits Per Month" and, new, "Verified ($)".
- `trueDeposits(doc)` reads `true_revenue_total` when `revenue_established` is true, otherwise N/A.
- A new `verifiedDeposits(doc)` reads `verified_revenue_total` when `verified_revenue_established` is true, otherwise N/A.
- Audit round 2, R2-OW03 (owner ruling 2026-10-02, the underwriter's Q3; §20): in the Both and True views the True cell ("True Deposits ($)", "Monthly Deposits ($)") carries a detail "Zelle excluded `<amount>`" where the statement's excluded Zelle total (its row's `non_revenue_by_reason.zelle_excluded`) is above 0, written through the row's own amount helper, so a non-USD row in a mixed-currency package names its unit (R2-B16's R51 unit rule then applies to it as to every amount of the row). The Total view has no True cell and no detail; a failed statement shows none.

The Settings text (`index.html:1507-1508`) becomes: "True revenue: every posted credit except known non-revenue (own-account transfers, funding, refunds) and the deposits held for review. The verified part, with positive proof, is shown beside it."

- The owner's amendment of 2026-10-06 to the underwriter's Q3 (R2-OW17; §20): the True cell's Zelle detail reads the row's `zelle_deposits` where it carries them (`monthlyZelleDetail`), through the row's own amount and unit: under Yes "Zelle in True `<amount>`", then " · held `<amount>`" and " · non-revenue `<amount>`" where there are some (a month whose Zelle is all held still shows it); under No "Zelle excluded `<amount>`", then " · counted after review `<amount>`" where there is some.

### 10.3 The chart

Each Total bar holds its True part, and the True part holds its Verified part, in three shades.
- Legend: "Total deposits", "True revenue", "of which verified".
- In the True view, the bar is True revenue, with its Verified part shaded.
- A statement whose revenue is not established draws no True or Verified part, and its labels read N/A.
- Audit fix batch B11 (I54, §20): in a package that refuses to combine its currencies (several, or one beside a member that declared none), the bars are scaled, and the peak chosen, within each currency (an undeclared member its own group), and every bar names its unit, USD included. Audit round 2, R2-B16 (R51, §20): the Monthly Statements table beside the chart (§10.2) names its units on the same rule (`unitsShown`, computed once in `renderMonthlyStatements` and handed to the chart): in such a package every declared row names its unit on its amount cells (Total, True, Verified and Monthly Deposits, and Ledger), USD included, in the Both, Total and True views, and an undeclared row stays bare, so there a bare figure means undeclared, never USD; a single-currency package's rows stay bare under the "($)" headers, and the headers, the count and NSF cells and an N/A cell carry no unit.

### 10.4 N/A rules (the D-1 fix)

The trace's D-1: the Verified Revenue cards print $0.00 or a partial figure where revenue is not established, and the package total adds such members in.
- A statement's True, Counted and Held figures show **N/A**, never $0.00, unless `revenue_established` is true: every posted credit carries a revenue state and a 5.6 tier, and the captured credits are the money the statement's Total counts. Its Verified figure shows N/A unless `verified_revenue_established` is true (today's condition, without the tier).
- The server computes both flags once, in `_displayed` for a statement and in `_package_analysis` for a package member, and the dashboard reads them. A statement with no captured credit and a zero Total is established at zero.
- A package's True, Counted and Held totals are N/A when any completed member's `revenue_established` is false, and its Verified total when any completed member's `verified_revenue_established` is false. The note under them names how many statements are not established ("2 of 6 statements have no established revenue"). A failed member is counted under `failed` as today; its credits are in no total. Audit round 2, R2-B15 (R54, §20): a package with no completed member has no True, Verified, Counted or Held figure at all (N/A, never $0.00), and a job still queued or processing is counted under `pending`, not `failed`.
- An outdated payload (before 5.6): True, Counted and Held are N/A, with the note "Re-analyze to compute true revenue". Verified shows the stored figure under the outdated notice. A package with an outdated member shows its True, Counted and Held totals as N/A, as for any member whose `revenue_established` is false.
- Audit fix batch B11 (I51, §20): the downloads follow the same rule. A statement download leaves empty, where `revenue_established` is false, True, Counted, Held and every name carrying them or a part of them (`true_revenue`, `true_revenue_total`/`_count`, the counted and held totals, counts and reasons, `revenue_review_items`, `unverified_deposit_total`, `potential_revenue_total`, `maximum_revenue`), and, where `verified_revenue_established` is false, Verified and its aliases (`confirmed_true_revenue`, `confirmed_true_revenue_total`). A package download leaves `maximum_revenue`, `potential_revenue_total`, `unverified_deposit_total` and `revenue_review_items` empty when a member is not established, and each document row its Verified figure (and alias) and its counted-plus-held figures under the same flags. Non-revenue stays: its rows are known non-revenue, captured rows only. The served payload is unchanged (the dashboard reads the flags).
- Audit round 2, R2-B16 (R52, §20): the CLI follows the same rule. Each account's flags are `analysis/revenue_view.py` `revenue_flags` over its serialized payload in the reading shown (`document_report_to_dict` over a document of that one account, which RULE S publishes as the account's payload; the L1-S3 census admits no other publisher), the flags the dashboard reads; the key lists of the rule above are `revenue_view.UNESTABLISHED_REVENUE_KEYS` and `UNESTABLISHED_VERIFIED_KEYS` (webapp/app.py imports them). `analyze.py` prints True, Counted, Held, Unverified and Maximum as "N/A (not established)" where `revenue_established` is false, and Verified where `verified_revenue_established` is; "Revenue reconciliation: Balanced" only where `reconciliation.ok` is true and the revenue is established (the dashboard's "Balanced", §10.1), otherwise "Review required (ledger does not reconcile)" or "Review required (captured credits differ from the bank-stated total)"; the four-tier identity on its own line, "Tiers sum to posted: yes (delta $x)". `analyze.py --json` writes the served copy (`apply_revenue_view` after the Zelle reading), so each account's metrics carry both flags and keep every figure. `batch.py` leaves `true_revenue_total`, `counted_flagged_total`, `excluded_pending_review_total`, `unverified_deposit_total` and `maximum_revenue` empty where the revenue is not established and `verified_revenue_total` where Verified is not, and its `needs_review` reads REVIEW where the revenue is not established.

### 10.5 Copy (`REVENUE_METRIC_COPY`)

- `trueRevenue`: "Posted credits minus known non-revenue and the deposits held for review"
- `verifiedRevenue`: "Revenue with proof: settlements, platform payouts, repeat or institutional payers, invoices, and deposits you confirmed"
- `countedFlagged`: "Counted in true revenue without proof of the payer: cash, checks, person-to-person, one-off payers"
- `heldForReview`: "Kept out of true revenue until you confirm it"
- `nonRevenue`: "Own-account transfers, funding, refunds and other known non-revenue"
- `totalCredits`, `achCredits`: unchanged.
- Audit fix batch B11 (I53, I34, I51, §20): `countedFlagged` becomes "Counted in true revenue without proof of the sale: cash, checks, person-to-person, wires, one-off, unlabelled and numbered-company payers, factoring and platform payouts" (the old note described 55% of counted dollars, and the payer is printed on most of them); `verifiedRevenue` becomes "Revenue with proof: card settlements, confirmed platform payouts, repeat or institutional payers, invoices, and deposits you confirmed"; `nonRevenueCaptured` is "Captured rows only: own-account transfers, funding, refunds and other known non-revenue". The Confirmed Withholding placeholder reads "Confirmed lender debits as a share of eligible deposits", and the Eligible Deposits card's note, on the default legacy basis, "Gross deposits less lender funding (not True revenue)" (copy only: the basis is the owner's I34).

Audit round 2, R2-OW03 (owner ruling 2026-10-02, the underwriter's Q3; §20): `nonRevenue` becomes "Own-account transfers, funding, refunds and other known non-revenue, Zelle deposits included" and `nonRevenueCaptured` "Captured rows only: own-account transfers, funding, refunds and other known non-revenue, Zelle deposits included".

Owner ruling 2026-10-02 (the underwriter's Q7; R2-OW14, §10.1, §20): the placeholders read "Confirmed lender debits as a share of the withholding basis (True revenue by default)" and "Possible lender debits as a share of the withholding basis (True revenue by default)", and the Withholding Basis card's placeholder "True revenue by default: verified plus counted credits"; the legacy note, "Gross deposits less lender funding (not True revenue)", stays for the legacy basis.

The side badge's title (`index.html:965`) becomes "Deposits held for review". The results-page sentence (`index.html:925`) becomes "Deposits held for review, and counted deposits, can be confirmed or excluded from the Review column." The outdated notice (`index.html:1179`) reads "Analysed with older classification rules." instead of "older lender rules", because it now covers revenue.

The owner's amendment of 2026-10-06 to the underwriter's Q3 (R2-OW17; §20): the Non-Revenue note drops ", Zelle deposits included" only where the served account or package says its Zelle deposits count in True revenue (`zelle_deposits.counted_as_true_revenue`, under Yes with Zelle); under No, and on a payload without the figures (which cannot say the mode), it is R2-OW03's. The Settings page's control reads "Mark Zelle Payments as True Revenue", its help: "Yes (default): Zelle deposits count in True revenue, flagged Zelle, with the person-to-person checks: Zelle from the business owner's own name, the same round amount repeated by one sender, and the other person-to-person checks (for example a sender the business also pays) are held for review; refunds, returns, loan money and asset sales stay out. No: every Zelle deposit is non-revenue, and its total is shown so you can compare True revenue with the Monthly Statements table. This changes True revenue, the review decision and the withholding rate on every statement and package analysed since this setting was added; nothing is reprocessed. An older analysis says so on its True card." Two labelled checkboxes driven as a radio pair (exactly one ticked; unticking the ticked one re-ticks it; both held while the choice loads or saves, and both unticked and held, with the error, when it cannot be read); a save says "Saved: Zelle deposits count as True revenue." or "Saved: Zelle deposits are non-revenue.", clears the decision dot of every Recent entry but the open one and redraws the open one.

### 10.6 Ledger tags, filters and chips

- `transactionCategory`: a verified credit is "Verified revenue" (VER, green), a counted one is "Counted: <reason label>" (CNT, teal), a held one is "Held: <reason label>" (?, amber), and a non-revenue one is "Non-revenue" (X, neutral). Reason labels come from the payload's reason code through one JS table that mirrors `REVENUE_TIER_REASONS`.
- A property-management verified row shows the chip "Property-management collections" (T15). A factoring credit keeps its "Flagged" chip.
- Filter pills (statement and modal): True Revenue, Verified, Counted, Held for Review, Non-Revenue. The `data-transaction-filter` values are `true_revenue`, `verified_revenue`, `counted_flagged`, `excluded_pending_review` and `non_revenue`.
- `revenueReviewReason` shows the reason label and one sentence for each code.
- Audit fix batch B11 (I53, §20): a counted reason's evidence row filters the ledger to that reason (`counted_flagged:<reason>`, headed "counted: <label>"), as a held reason's does (`excluded_pending_review:<reason>`).
- Audit round 2, R2-OW03 (owner ruling 2026-10-02; §20): a `non_revenue` row that carries a non-revenue code (§5.3) is tagged "Non-revenue: <label>" ("Non-revenue: Zelle deposit (excluded by policy)", "Non-revenue: Government payment, no purpose printed"; R2-OW06, the underwriter's Q11 (b): "Non-revenue: Sale of equipment or vehicles (not a dealer)") and `revenueReviewReason` gives "<label>. <sentence>"; a reviewer's rejection keeps its counted or held code and reads "Non-revenue" as before. A code's evidence sub-row filters the ledger to it (`non_revenue:<code>`, headed "excluded: <label>").

- Owner ruling 2026-10-02 (the underwriter's Q5; R2-OW13, §20): a returned funder payment's debit carries a "Returned" chip, and its return credit says "Returns the <date> payment to <funder>" under its reason, a held one included (its tier and reason unchanged). The lender filter still reads the withholding flag, so the returned rows stay in it.
- Owner ruling 2026-10-02 (the underwriter's Q6; R2-OW15, §20): in the package ledger a deposit the package took out of True reads "Returned on <date> (<file>): not counted. Confirm Revenue overrides the match." under its reason, its return "Returns the <date> deposit in <file>.", and a return left unmatched because the analyst confirmed its nearest deposit "Matches the <date> deposit you confirmed in <file>; review."; a statement viewed alone shows none. The filters `packageMatch:<kind>` (a match's rows, both legs, headed "bounced deposits matched across statements") and `debitFlag:<kind>` (a flag's debits, headed "returned deposits not matched" or "processor chargebacks and adjustments") show them.
- Owner ruling 2026-10-02 (the underwriter's Q4; R2-OW16, §20): in the package ledger a deposit pass 2 held reads "Transfer out of <bank> ••<last4> on <date> (<file>), <n> day(s) earlier. Confirm Revenue releases it into True and marks it Verified; Mark Non-Revenue keeps it out." under its reason ("the same day" for a gap of 0), an already-held deposit that matches "Also matches a transfer out of <bank> ••<last4> on <date> (<file>).", and the transfer out "Matched to the <date> deposit into ••<last4> (held)." or "(already held)."; the held reason's sentence says the same. A statement viewed alone shows none.

- The owner's amendment of 2026-10-06 to the underwriter's Q3 (R2-OW17; §20): under Yes a row the served payload tags `zelle_deposit` shows a "Zelle" chip beside its reason tag, on the statement's and the package's ledgers (the owner's "flagged 'Zelle'"); its reason tag stays the rules' ("Person-to-person", "From the holder's own name or brand", "Repeated round sums from one sender", ...). Under No the ledger is R2-OW03's.

### 10.7 The review queue

- **What needs review now:** the held rows. The side badge counts `revenue_review_items` (the held count), and a "Held for Review" view groups them by reason, largest total first.
- **The funding aid** (the underwriter's Q1 (2026-10-02); §8.5; R2-OW12). A held no-sender wire's row shows one line per series under its reason (`fundingSeriesNotes`, beside R2-B07's unread payer blocks), in the ledger, the statement window and the package ledger, its money in the row's currency:
  - start observed: "Recurring payments start after this deposit: possible funding. Weekly $1,250.00 to <payee> from <date> (2 days after, 3 payments)."
  - start not observable: "Recurring payments follow this deposit: possible funding. … ; the statement begins too close to this deposit to show whether they ran before it."

  A decided row shows no aid, nor does any other row or a payload analysed before the field. The badge, the Held for Review grouping and the gate do not read it; the underwriter decides through Confirm Revenue and Mark Non-Revenue.
- **What may be reviewed:**
  - Held and counted rows show Confirm Revenue and Mark Non-Revenue.
  - A rule-verified row shows Mark Non-Revenue only (T6).
  - A decided row shows its decision and Reset Decision.
  - Non-revenue rows have no controls (§15), with one exception (audit round 2, R2-OW03; owner ruling 2026-10-02, the underwriter's Q3, "I can review"): a `zelle_excluded` row shows Confirm Revenue only. Confirm sets it `verified_revenue`, tier `verified` (the deposits you confirmed; the Verified badge on it is the reviewer's proof, not the rules', and Q4's "never Verified" is about the rules), its reason kept; reset restores `non_revenue` / `zelle_excluded`, status `not_required`; replay keeps a confirm. It is never pending and never in the multi-select. Every other `non_revenue` row, a Q12 government payment that prints no purpose and a Q11 (b) `asset_sale_proceeds` row included (R2-OW06; §17.1, the asset-sale follow-up (2)), keeps no control.
- **The server** (`analysis/revenue.py` `record_serialized_revenue_review`):
  - allowed initial states become `unverified_deposit` and `verified_revenue`;
  - `confirm` on a row whose initial state is `verified_revenue` is refused ("already verified");
  - confirm sets tier `verified`, reject sets tier `non_revenue`, and reset restores `revenue_initial_classification` and `revenue_initial_tier`;
  - the reason is kept for the audit;
  - R2-OW03: a tiered row whose initial state is `non_revenue` and whose reason is in `REVIEWABLE_NON_REVENUE_REASONS` (`zelle_excluded` alone) takes a confirm and a reset; a reject on it is refused with the non-revenue refusal ("only automatically unverified deposits can be reviewed"), the row being non-revenue already, so the writer and the replay agree.
- **Storage:** `webapp/jobs.py` records the full classification as `prior_state` today, so the tier fields reach the audit without a schema change. `review_decisions` is unchanged.
- **Replay:** `webapp/reanalysis.py` `_awaits_review` becomes decision-aware, `_awaits_review(record, decision)`:
  - a row whose initial state is `unverified_deposit` awaits any decision, as today;
  - a row whose initial state is `verified_revenue` (decided by a rule) awaits only a `reject`: the analyst's word wins over a rule, so the reject is replayed;
  - a `confirm` on a row whose initial state is `verified_revenue` does not await review. `replay_reviews` puts it in `ruled`, reported under `reviews_decided_by_rules`, as today. It never reaches the review writer, which would refuse it ("already verified") and report it as needing redoing;
  - R2-OW03: a `zelle_excluded` row awaits a `confirm` only: a stored confirm is replayed, and a stored reject (the writer refuses it on a row already non-revenue) is reported as decided by the rules.
- **The multi-select batch** (`/analysis/<job_id>/revenue-reviews`) takes the same rows.
- **A deposit the package took out of True** (the underwriter's Q6 (2026-10-02); §6.2's package passes; R2-OW15) keeps its initial state (`unverified_deposit`) and its pending status in the overlay, so it shows Confirm Revenue and Mark Non-Revenue in the package ledger. Each is the statement's own decision, written by the review routes and replayed on re-analysis as every decision is: Confirm sets it Verified and overrides the match (a decided credit is never matched), Mark agrees it is not revenue, and Reset restores the rule and the match. Nothing else is stored.
- **A deposit the package held as a transfer between the business's accounts** (the underwriter's Q4 (2026-10-02), "listed so it can be released"; §6.2's package passes; R2-OW16) is released by **Confirm Revenue**: it is the statement's own decision, like the row above, so the deposit turns Verified on its own statement and in every package that holds it (§10.7's existing behaviour for every held row: the release counts as the analyst's verification, although Q2 of 2026-09-28 never lets a rule verify a bare deposit), and a decided credit is never matched again. Mark Non-Revenue keeps it out; Reset restores the rule and the hold. A release that restores the row's earlier counted tier would need a new decision kind in the route, the store and the replay (§17.1).
- **An outdated payload (before 5.6)** is reviewed under today's rules. Its records carry no tier, so the server writes no tier field. Only `unverified_deposit` rows are reviewable, confirm sets `verified_revenue` and reject sets `non_revenue`. Its rebuild takes the tier-less path of §12.

- **Decisions on a Zelle row, in both readings** (the owner's amendment of 2026-10-06 to the underwriter's Q3; R2-OW17, §20). A decision is validated on the reading the reviewer sees, and the latest decision on a posting sets every reading: a reading that accepts it takes it, and a reading that refuses it returns to its analysis state. Both routes read the setting once per request and write through `analysis/zelle_view.py` `with_both_readings`: the reading shown takes every decision of the request or none (all or nothing, as the batch route is); the other reading takes each decision on its own, a refused one there becoming a `reset` (and a refused reset leaves it as it is, at its analysis state); one `reviewed_at` is written to both; both are rebuilt and the edits computed again. Under Yes a Zelle row's initial state is `unverified_deposit`, so it shows Confirm Revenue and Mark Non-Revenue and joins the multi-select; under No it shows Confirm Revenue only (R2-OW03). A reject taken in Yes rejects the counted reading and resets the stored one (`zelle_excluded`, `not_required`, still offering Confirm; an earlier confirm there is cleared, never left Verified); a confirm in either mode verifies both; a reset returns each to its own analysis reading; a reject in No is refused, as before (the valve). An account whose edits are unusable takes today's path and loses the key. The audit row's `prior_state` is the record of the reading shown (`JobStore.apply_review`/`apply_reviews` take the reading, materialised once per call). The re-analysis replay applies the same rule to the fresh analysis: the latest decision per posting is written to each reading whose record awaits it, every other reading staying at its analysis state; it is replayed when any reading takes it, refused only when every reading that awaits it refuses it, and decided by the rules only when no reading awaits it. A payload without edits keeps today's replay exactly. A copy whose only decision lives in the counted reading's edits (a Yes-mode reject) still ranks as decided (`_copy_rank`).

### 10.8 Exports

- **Statement CSV/XLSX:** the new metric keys flatten as today. The by-reason dicts are written as readable rows through the escaped-row path: section `revenue_tier`, field `<tier>.<reason>.count` / `.total`. A row's classification record, in evidence, carries its tier fields.
- **Package CSV/XLSX:** totals and document rows gain the keys of §9.2. The per-state evidence sections are unchanged, and each record carries its tier fields. The currency sweep covers the new money keys and the by-reason totals.
- **JSON:** follows the displayed payload.
- Audit fix batch B11 (I32, I52, I51, §20):
  - **Statement CSV/XLSX:** after the flat rows, one row per posted credit: a `posted_credit,columns,…` row, then `posted_credit,<n>,date,description,amount,currency,tier,reason,state,review_status` (codes as the payload has them); each account of a document has its own block under its section prefix.
  - **Package CSV/XLSX:** one evidence section per tier: `verified_revenue_evidence_N`, `counted_flagged_evidence_N`, `excluded_pending_review_evidence_N`, `non_revenue_evidence_N` (a credit of a member analysed before 5.6 carries no tier and stays in `unverified_deposit_evidence_N`), each record carrying `source_currency` and `source_account`; after the flat rows, the combined ledger, one posting a row (`package_transaction,<n>,source_document,source_account,source_currency,date,description,amount,classification,tier,reason,state,review_status`).
  - **XLSX cells are typed:** a bool is a boolean cell, a finite int or float a number; NaN, inf and every numeric-looking string stay text, and text stays an inline string (never a formula) whose formula guard's apostrophe is literal, kept so a Save As CSV stays inert.
  - **Empty where not established:** §10.4's download rule.
- Audit round 2, R2-B14 (R16, R14, §20): **Package CSV/XLSX:** a left-out repeat's row carries `duplicate_kept_because`; a left-out shorter printout's row adds `duplicate_reason_words` ("a shorter printout of days another statement covers"), a left-out printout of more than a month's the review round's words ("a printout of more than a month whose every row other statements of the account print"); each pair of overlapping statements that share credits is a section `overlapping_statement_<n>` (its keys, its `currency` among them, then `words`: "`<file>` and `<file>` share `<n>` credit(s) (`<money> <currency>`) in the days both cover, counted in both", the money without a unit when the pair's currency is unknown), the notice's words.
- Audit round 2, R2-B15 (R15, R55, §20): **Package CSV/XLSX:** each account left out of every figure for another reason than a repeat is a section `excluded_account_<n>` (`job_id`, `filename`, `account_index`, `account_count`, `outcome`, `reason`), after the duplicate groups; the totals carry `completeness` and `excluded_account_count` beside it, and `pending` when a job is still on its way. `monthly_lender_debits` is the lender debits per calendar month (it was the package's total), and a package with no statement analysed leaves its True, Verified, Counted and Held cells empty (R54).
- Audit round 2, R2-B16 (R53, §20): **Statement CSV/XLSX:** after the posted-credit table, one row per posted debit (a debit not marked unposted): a `posted_debit,columns,…` row, then `posted_debit,<n>,date,description,amount,currency,classification,flagged_group,canonical_entity,review_required,returned_funder_payment` (the amount signed and numeric; `flagged_group` only where Settings shows the group, `flag_shown`, otherwise empty; `returned_funder_payment` the location of the credit that returned a confirmed funder's payment unpaid, R2-OW13's `returned_funder_payment_by`, otherwise empty), each account of a document under its section prefix, through the escaped-row path. **XLSX only:** a text cell over the spreadsheet's 32,767-character limit (counted in UTF-16 units, as Excel counts it: a character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane counts two) is replaced whole by "Not shown: `<N>` characters, over the spreadsheet cell limit; see the JSON download." and never cut (Excel refuses such a file at a normal load, and its repair cuts the cell); this is the ledger cell (`statement.transactions`) on most statements and a large evidence list on some. The writer is shared, so a package XLSX cell over the limit reads the same pointer; a cell up to the limit is written as before. The CSV keeps every JSON cell whole, and the JSON downloads, the flat rows and their order, the credit table, cell typing and the formula guard are unchanged.
- Audit round 2, R2-OW03 (owner ruling 2026-10-02, §20): **Statement and package CSV/XLSX:** the non-revenue breakdown is written as the by-reason dicts are (`_TIER_REASON_KEYS`): section `revenue_tier` (a package's document rows `document_<n>.revenue_tier`), field `non_revenue.<code>.count` / `.total`; never left empty where revenue is not established, and a refused package's totals print the counts and no money.
- Owner ruling 2026-10-02 (the underwriter's Q6; R2-OW15, §20): **Package CSV/XLSX:** each match the package passes made is a section `package_match_<n>` (`kind`, `moved`, its `credit` and `debit` as JSON, `gap_days`) and each flagged debit a section `debit_flag_<n>` (`kind`, `wording`, `candidate_decided`, `source_job`, `source_document`, `source_account`, `source_currency`, `source_location`, `date`, `amount`, `description`), after the overlapping statements, through the escaped-row path; the totals and document rows carry §9.2's keys where they are published. **Statement CSV/XLSX:** the served flag keys (§9.1) flatten as metric rows where a debit is flagged.
- Owner ruling 2026-10-02 (the underwriter's Q4; R2-OW16, §20): **Package CSV/XLSX:** each transfer pair is a `package_match_<n>` section too (`kind` `own_account_transfer`, `moved` true or false), and the totals carry `own_account_transfer_held_count` / `_total` and `own_account_transfer_already_held_count` / `_total` where published (a refused package writes the counts and no money).

- **The Zelle figures and tag** (the owner's amendment of 2026-10-06 to the underwriter's Q3; R2-OW17, §20). The generic metrics, totals and document loops skip `zelle_deposits`; where it is present it is written as readable rows of the `revenue_tier` sections (the statement's and the package's `revenue_tier`, a document row's `document_<n>.revenue_tier`): `zelle_deposits.setting` (Yes or No), `.count`, `.total`, `.<tier>.count`, `.<tier>.total` and `.setting_applied`; a refused total is an empty cell. The posted-credit table and the package ledger table gain a trailing `zelle` column only in a block where a row carries the tag, 'Zelle' on those rows; the JSON downloads, the package's `transactions` and `analyze --json` keep the `zelle_deposit` key. **Under No, against today** (the closed list): an account with a confirmed Zelle deposit, a legacy account or one whose setting is not applied serves `zelle_deposits` (and the package and document figures, the readable rows and the True card's parts follow); the Settings page and `/api/settings` show the choice; the batch CSV's three Zelle columns (§13) are a fixed header. Every other No output of a fresh analysis, and every Zelle-free download, is byte-identical to today's.

- **Lender payment changes** (the owner's request of 2026-10-06; R2-OW18, §20). The statement downloads write a `lender_payment_change_<n>` section per item (`LENDER_PAYMENT_CHANGE_EXPORT_FIELDS`, with `schedule_confirmed` and `via`, and the dotted notes; R2-OW18 review round 1 adds `first_after_kind`, `resumed_date` and `last_step_percent`, and a `via` cell names each level's step, "weekly 950.0 (-5%)"), never a JSON cell for the key; the package's add `source_document`, `from_document`, `to_document`, `cross_statement`, `source_currency`, `source_period_end` and `continues_in_other_account.*`, and a `lender_payment_unchecked_<n>` section (`source_document`, `reason`) per member not checked across statements. Each section is statement-level, in its item's own unit; the JSON downloads carry both keys.

## 11. Withholding

- **Default: `true_revenue`** (owner ruling 2026-10-02, the underwriter's Q7, "2 Make True revenue the default"; T8 amended; R2-OW14, §20). True revenue, verified plus counted credits, divides the confirmed withholding rate and the potential exposure (`DEFAULT_WITHHOLDING_DENOMINATOR_MODE`). `load_settings` reads an unset, empty or unknown `WITHHOLDING_DENOMINATOR_MODE` as it, and `Settings`, `compute_metrics` and the `Metrics` dataclass take it. The tryout host sets no mode, so it divides by True revenue. A statement whose True revenue is $0 has no rate and sets `withholding_review_required` (its note: "withholding rate is unavailable because True revenue is zero or missing"), whether or not it pays a lender; a review that confirms held credits restores the rate. Until this ruling the default was `legacy_eligible_deposits`, and this spec had given no reason to move it.
- **Selectable:** `legacy_eligible_deposits` (effective deposits minus lender (financing-proceeds) credits, less internal-transfer credits in a package) and `verified_revenue` (unchanged, Q1), through `WITHHOLDING_DENOMINATOR_MODE`. `legacy_eligible_deposits` stays published on every statement, whatever the mode.
- **A stored payload** whose metrics carry no mode was analysed on the legacy basis and keeps it: `normalize_withholding_denominator_mode`'s own default stays `legacy_eligible_deposits`, so the review rebuild, the package and the dashboard read it as legacy. The settings key changes with the default, so every cached analysis is recomputed on its next read (R2-B16's stage bump forces it too); a package whose members were analysed under different modes reads "Mixed denominator configuration" until they are recomputed.
- **G7** (§14.3) pins the legacy basis in the lender census's snapshot (`tools/lender_census.py`), so it compares one basis across trees and the switch is a declared product change, never a lender-figure move.
- **Package internal transfers in the `true_revenue` mode.** `_package_analysis` deducts R-d's internal-transfer credits from the legacy denominator only (`webapp/app.py:1478`). The verified mode needs no deduction, because an internal-transfer credit is `non_revenue` and was never in it. That reasoning does not hold for True revenue: an R-d pair can include a credit a member counted (a named transfer between two members, `p2p`). In the `true_revenue` mode, the package deducts the R-d internal-transfer credits whose tier is `verified` or `counted_flagged`, and only those.
- **The numerator** (owner ruling 2026-10-02, the underwriter's Q5; R2-OW13, §20): the confirmed lender debits paid plus the funder payments returned unpaid, every row that `contributes_to_withholding_rate`: a bounced scheduled payment leaves paid to lenders but stays in the rate, the obligation standing. The package sums its members' numerators. The ruling left the basis as it was; the underwriter's Q7 (2026-10-02) moved its default (above).
- **How the figures relate.** Every financing-proceeds credit is `non_revenue`, so when a statement's line items are its Total, True revenue ≤ legacy eligible deposits. The gap is the other non-revenue (own-account transfers, refunds, insurance, potential-lender credits, duplicates) plus the held credits. Verified ≤ True always.
- **Package matches in the True and Verified modes** (owner ruling 2026-10-02, the underwriter's Q6; R2-OW15, §6.2's package passes, §20). A deposit the package passes take out of True leaves the revenue basis it was in: in the `true_revenue` mode each member's denominator loses its moved credits stored `verified` or `counted_flagged`, in the `verified_revenue` mode those stored `verified_revenue` (none in practice: a deposit-channel credit is never verified by a rule, and a confirmed one is never matched). The legacy basis and the numerator are untouched, and each statement viewed alone keeps its own rate. Owner ruling 2026-10-02 (the underwriter's Q4; R2-OW16): a deposit pass 2 holds as a transfer between the business's accounts is such a moved credit (stored `counted_flagged`), so the `true_revenue` mode loses it and the `verified_revenue` mode, which never held it, does not; an already-held deposit pass 2 only annotates never moves the basis.
- **Where eligible deposits move:**
  - down, where `SQ CAP` and SBA or EIDL credits become financing proceeds (§7.11);
  - up, where Q7 takes dealer funding out of D1 (§8.7).

  Both moves are listed in the census.

- **The Zelle reading** (the owner's amendment of 2026-10-06 to the underwriter's Q3; R2-OW17, §20). The counted reading's metrics are `compute_metrics`' own, with the same arguments, so the setting moves True and Verified, the gate, the held items, the True-revenue withholding rate on R2-OW14's default basis (a statement's 'withholding rate is unavailable because True revenue is zero or missing' note leaves where Yes lifts True off $0), each potential lender's denominator and exposure, the package's member denominators and the monthly figures, exactly. The legacy basis's rate never moves: its eligible deposits read no tier. One lender fact follows the reading: a bounce-worded Zelle credit the rules count stays unpaired in Yes, so pass 7b (§6.2) leaves its funder debit paid (corpus: none).

- **Lender payment changes** (the owner's request of 2026-10-06; R2-OW18, §20): payment changes never enter the numerator, the basis or the rate; they are information only.

## 12. Backward compatibility

- **Stored analyses are never rewritten.** A saved job keeps its payload until someone re-analyzes it, and the Re-analyze route (lender spec §8.6) replays review decisions as today, with §10.7's widening.
- **Outdated notice:** automatic for every analysis older than the running version (§9.3).
- **Before 5.6:** no tiers. The served copy:
  - sets `revenue_established` false;
  - sets `true_revenue`, `true_revenue_total` and the tier totals to `None`;
  - sets every `true_revenue_evidence` to `None`: in each account's metrics and detection, and in the package's top level and `detection`;
  - removes `contributes_to_true_revenue` from every row's classification record, so a reader never takes the old verified meaning for the new one;
  - keeps `verified_revenue_*` as stored (T10).
  The stored job is untouched: `_displayed` copies before it changes anything, as `apply_flagged_groups_to_payload` does.
- **The tier-less rebuild path.** A review on a pre-5.6 job rebuilds its revenue views (`rebuild_serialized_revenue_views`). When no record in the payload carries `revenue_tier`, the rebuild runs today's three-state logic: it computes no tier totals, skips the state/tier agreement check, and leaves `revenue_established` false. A payload in which some records carry a tier and others do not is refused, as a missing state is refused today. The review writer follows §10.7's outdated rules.
- **Gating an outdated member.** Its held rows cannot be told from its counted ones, so T7's held share cannot be computed. An outdated member is gated by today's rule: it needs revenue review when it has a pending `unverified_deposit` row, a direction conflict, or revenue that does not reconcile. The package note names it ("Re-analyze to compute true revenue").
- **Field names** (T9):
  - kept with their meaning: `revenue_classification`, `verified_revenue_*`, `unverified_deposit_*`, `non_revenue_*`, `maximum_revenue`, `revenue_initial_classification`, `revenue_review_status`, `confirmed_true_revenue*` (Verified) and `potential_revenue*` (unverified);
  - repointed: `true_revenue`, `contributes_to_true_revenue` and `true_revenue_evidence`, to the new True revenue;
  - changed in meaning and stated: `revenue_review_required`, on a row and in metrics (T7), and `manual_review`;
  - new: everything in §9.
- **`LEGACY_REVENUE_STATE_MAP`** (`true_revenue` → `verified_revenue`, `potential_revenue` → `unverified_deposit`) keeps reading records from before version 3.0. It maps stored **state** strings, not metric names, so repointing the `true_revenue` metric does not touch it.

- **Analyses stored before the Zelle setting** (the owner's amendment of 2026-10-06 to the underwriter's Q3; R2-OW17, §9.1, §20). One with Zelle policy rows and no edits (analysed between R2-OW02 and R2-OW17) is served as stored in both modes; under Yes its `setting_applied` is false and the True card says "analysed before the Zelle setting: shown as analysed". A **legacy** account (analysed before R2-OW02, its Zelle natively counted, no policy row) is served as stored in both modes; under No its `setting_applied` is false with the same notice, so the No choice never silently fails to apply. Until R2-B16's stage bump, a re-analysis or a fresh upload of a cached statement returns the cached payload unchanged (the analysis stage's key carries `ANALYSIS_STAGE_VERSION`, which R2-OW17 does not bump), so neither adds the edits; nothing promises it. From R2-B16's bump on, a re-analysis computes both readings.

- **Analyses stored before the lender payment check** (the owner's request of 2026-10-06; R2-OW18, §20): a payload without `detection.lender_payment_changes` is never computed at serve time; it shows "not checked" where lender rows exist, and a package lists such a member as `analysed_before_check` and leaves it out of its chains (a job still queued or processing is `not_ready`). Its records carry no `potential_payee_key`.

### 14.2 The census (`tools/revenue_census.py`, local only)

The census re-classifies every cached analysis at the base (5.4), at 5.5 and at 5.6. It uses the account filter of `tools/lender_census.py` (reconciled, de-duplicated by statement fingerprint) and never drops `non_revenue` rows. Its output is digit-masked and stays in the private research folder.

For the tryout host, the same tool runs read-only against a copy of the host's job store. This is the per-row dump both government and AP verifiers asked for, because the existing tryout dump is grouped by payer and holds no `non_revenue` rows.

It reports, for each run:
- True share, Verified share, and the count of statements at $0 for each; the median statement share;
- the dollars and rows in each tier and each reason code;
- a move matrix, from each base (state, rule) to each new (tier, reason), in dollars, rows and statements;
- every row that left `non_revenue`, grouped by the narrowing of §6.3 that moved it; any row outside those nine (and OQ2's ruling) is a failure;
- every row that went from verified to anything else, grouped by declared cause (§7.0, §7.11); any other cause is a failure;
- `lender_credits` and eligible-deposit moves by cause (§11);
- the package gate's blocked share before and after (T7), and each hold's contribution to it;
- the sizes behind T4, T11, T13, T18 and T19, and how much of `named_payer_unlabelled` would pass Q6;
- the holds the memo's rows could not measure: `payer_also_debited`, `payer_debited_as_lender`, `insurer_payer` and the released card credits held as `possible_return`;
- every row the channel gate and the holder veto demoted under 5.5, by rule;
- every credit whose `normalized_description` the street-`LN` guard changed, with its base and new decision (G7b);
- (audit round 2, R2-B01) every account whose parse changed between the two snapshots, with its bank, parser route, rows, dollars and the True delta of its moved rows, totalled by bank (G18); the rows that moved with the parse are compared apart from the rules' moves;
- (audit round 2, R2-B01) the unreconciled accounts the filter leaves out (their count, banks, posted credits and tiers), and every account that reconciles in one snapshot only, both ways, with its True;
- (owner ruling 2026-10-02, Q12) in the sweep of the non-revenue wording left in True (B1's classes A to H), class G also reads the seven no-purpose government forms of §6.1 step 3a, on the masked text with the receiver read past and nothing after the form but the reader's own words; the Treasury form is read at medium confidence, since the masked agency code cannot be read. Class H ("unclear, owner") keeps only the forms the ruling did not name (another state's `STATE MMB`, another agency's Treasury `MISC PAY` the class-G wording does not read, another province, another workers' compensation board, Quebec's other payments) and a named form printing a word the reader does not read.

Since audit round 2 (R2-B01), the census's primary basis is a re-parse: `snapshot --reparse` (in this tool and in `tools/lender_census.py`) re-parses every latest analysis input that a cached OCR reading reaches with the checkout's deterministic analysis stage (no model, no network), and reads every other input from the cache; the snapshot counts the inputs re-parsed, failed and read from the cache. Each credit records its raw parse (a hash of its digit-masked printed description and its cents) and each account its parse over every row, so `compare` tells a parse's move from a rule's.

The owner's amendment of 2026-10-06 to the underwriter's Q3 (R2-OW17, §20): `snapshot --zelle-true-revenue {yes,no}` (default yes, the Settings default) classifies in that reading where the checkout takes it (`classify_statement_transactions`' keyword, guarded for `--code-root`; the guard facts' `progress_draw` follows it), records it at the top level (`zelle_true_revenue`: true, false, or null on a checkout without the setting, which reads as its one reading: No from R2-OW02 on) and records each credit's `zelle_prior` from the stored reading. `compare` refuses snapshots of different readings (`ZelleViewMismatch`, beside `BasisMismatch`) unless `--declare-zelle-view`; with it, a credit whose base method is the Zelle policy's and whose tier, reason or state moves takes the declared cause `zelle_true_revenue_view`, whether it leaves `non_revenue` or not. It is no §6.3 narrowing (the closed list is unchanged) and never a G1 failure; G-Z checks it (§14.3). A non-Zelle credit whose Q5 or Q6 repeat partner is a Zelle sale or draw in the after snapshot takes the existing cause `q5_q6_q11_repeat_partner`. A base Yes, after No compare declares the reverse moves through `zelle_policy` and the move matrix.

### 14.3 Guard checks (hard gates)

No loan, transfer, refund or owner money becomes revenue:
- **G1:** no row decided `non_revenue` by reversal, the insurer registry, D1, descriptor proceeds, the potential registry, strong non-revenue, duplicates or (owner ruling 2026-10-02, Q12) step 3a's government payments at the base reaches True at 5.6, except through the narrowings of §6.3 that lead to True (1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7 and, audit fix batch B3, 9: counted, never verified; and, owner ruling 2026-10-02, the underwriter's Q2, 13: a listed insurer's credit paid for the business's work, counted, never verified, the census's `15_insurer_paid_for_services`), each listed.
- **G2:** no Verified row carries a financing root, read as T4 reads it (§8.1: on the payer region and the entry fields, after the posting labels are removed), except a Q7 row whose payer is a listed auto lender or a credit union under §8.7's credit-union arm (G12 checks that).
- **G3:** no row the holder test matches (§5.2, read on the payer region) is Verified by step 11's customer and invoice descriptors, steps 12 to 14, Q5 or Q6, and none is `counted_flagged`. The only rows the holder test matches that may be in True are those the registry (step 10) or a card-settlement or claim-payment form verified; the census lists them, and they join the precision sample (§14.5).
- **G4:** no row with transfer wording and no counterparty is in True.
- **G5:** no row that `match_known_payee` places in a financing group reaches True, except payout-credit entities, factoring payees and Q7's dealer funding, and (owner ruling 2026-10-02, Q9 (c'); audit round 2, R2-OW05) a listed auto lender's payables-only credit the pass counts as `lender_paid_for_services` (§8.7: its method is exempt; G2 still fails any Verified row with a financing root, so it is never Verified). The census declares its demotion `q7_payables_without_dealer_evidence`: a base Verified row of method `auto_lender_dealer_funding` whose later method is `lender_paid_for_services`, counted, or held as `financing_named_payer` under the hidden-loan guard.
- **G6:** no row whose revenue method is `direction_conflict` is in True.
- **G7:** `tools/lender_census.py` at 5.6 shows zero lender, potential-lender and flag changes on debits against 5.4. Owner ruling 2026-10-02 (the underwriter's Q5; R2-OW13): the snapshot records `withholding_numerator`, `lender_count_entities` and `returned_funder_rows`, and compare declares `returned_funder_moves` (a withholding-row move on a row the after snapshot lists as returned, never counted outside the allowlist), `kept_in_count_returned` (a funder whose every paid row was returned and that stays in the lender count, never `lost`), the paid rows that leave the lenders list (`paid_rows`: for a returned row or not), the lender count's moves and the withholding numerator's; every other withholding or `reversed_by` move outside the owner's allowlist still fails. Owner ruling 2026-10-02 (the underwriter's Q7; R2-OW14): the snapshot computes its metrics on the legacy basis (`withholding_denominator_mode="legacy_eligible_deposits"`, named explicitly), so `eligible_deposits` and `withholding_rate` compare one basis across trees whatever the analysis's default.
- **G7b:** every credit whose normalized text the street-`LN` guard changed is listed with its base and new decision; none moved from a financing decision to True.
- **G8:** every fabricated negative of §14.1 passes.
- **G9:** the four-tier identity holds on every cached analysis.
- **G10:** no Verified row prints a consumer person-to-person rail, a check-deposit form, a cash, branch or ATM form, or no payer word at all; a Verified row that prints a real-time or push rail was verified by the registry (§6.1 step 9b).
- **G11:** no row that prints the pay words of Q8 (§8.1 `payroll_or_salary`) or the personal-income words (§8.1 `personal_income`) is in True.
- **G12:** every `auto_lender_dealer_funding` row's payer, read on its originator segment, is a listed auto lender, or a credit union with two or more `VHCL PURCH` credits in the statement (§8.7), and the row prints no loan, proceeds, advance or refund word.
- **G13:** no row whose payer region §5.2's numbered-company guard matches is Verified.
- **G14:** no row the channel gate closed, or that a `DEBIT CARD CREDIT` or `POS CREDIT` label names, is counted toward any recurrence pool.
- **G18** (audit round 2, R2-B01): every account whose parse changed between the two snapshots (a credit whose printed row or amount changed, a credit with no partner, or a changed parse over every row) is explained: by a note of the source check that explains it, or, when both snapshots were re-parsed, by its parser route. Its moved rows are read only by the guards that read the later row alone, never by G1, G7b or a demotion cause.
- **G19** (owner ruling 2026-10-02, Q12): no counted or Verified credit prints one of the six non-Treasury no-purpose government forms of §6.1 step 3a with no purpose, read on the masked text past the statement furniture as the sweep's class G reads it. The Treasury form is reported in the sweep's medium column, never gated: on masked text another agency's `12 TREAS 310 MISC PAY`, which the classifier keeps, cannot be told from the VA's 36.
- **G20** (owner ruling 2026-10-02, the underwriter's Q10; R2-OW11): no credit of a premium trust account is verified or counted. Each account records whether its printed title reads PREMIUM TRUST (`premium_trust`, the metrics' fact, never the title's words); the guard reads no row fact, and a snapshot written before R2-OW11 carries no flag, so it cannot fail there. The compare declares a verified credit pass 7 holds there (`premium_trust_account`: the later method `premium_trust_account`).

- **G-Z** (the owner's amendment of 2026-10-06 to the underwriter's Q3; R2-OW17), beside G1 on a compare that declares the Zelle reading (base No, after Yes): every Zelle policy row's counted (tier, reason) is its base `zelle_prior`, except on a premium trust account (after reason `premium_trust_account`), under $1 (the floor), on a lifted carve-out (after reason `asset_sale_proceeds` or `construction_progress_draw`) and on a Zelle row whose Q5 or Q6 repeat partner is a lifted carve-out row (its prior verified, the after counted). Any other difference fails, and so does any non-Zelle credit that moves between the readings (but a verified one whose demotion is `q5_q6_q11_repeat_partner`): the lessor fact keeps its Zelle skip, so nothing else may move. A base without `zelle_prior` leaves its rows unchecked, and the report counts them. **G7 in both readings:** `tools/lender_census.py snapshot --zelle-true-revenue {yes,no}` (default yes) records the reading and each account's `zelle_policy_rows`; `compare` refuses mixed readings unless `--declare-zelle-view`, which classes a funder debit's lender-totals row or returned-payment entry that moves because its return credit is a Zelle policy row as `zelle_reading_rule_d` (pass 7b follows the reading) and fails every other lender, withholding, potential, reversal, lender-count or eligible-deposit move.

- **G7's new outputs** (the owner's request of 2026-10-06; R2-OW18): the lender census's snapshot gains one key, `lender_payment_changes` (each statement's items as `[kind, lender, state, position, cadence, cadence after, change percent, stop confirmed]`; absent on a checkout without the module), and its compare a `lender_payment_changes` block (counts by kind and state after and in the base, the accounts not comparable, the items gained and lost): new outputs only, never in the exit condition and never added to an existing figure. Every existing output reads its zero value, and the snapshot with the key removed (`without_payment_changes`) is byte-identical to the base.

The census replaces every one of them.

### 14.5 Precision sample (before merge)

The census proves that nothing moved outside the declared paths. It cannot prove that what a new rule verifies is revenue. Before merge, an independent reviewer hand-sorts a stratified sample from the 5.6 census, digit-masked and kept in the private folder:
- about 200 Verified rows, at least 20 from each of: Q5 repeat wires; Q6 (a) repeats; Q6 (b) company form; Q6 (c) government and healthcare; §7.5 accounts-payable remittance; §7.6 public payers; §7.9 invoice wires; the card forms and payout forms of §7.1 and §7.2; Q7 (every Q7 row if fewer than 20); and the holder-test rows G3 lists;
- the 50 largest `counted_flagged` rows of the corpus, whatever their reason.

Each row is sorted as revenue, not revenue (naming which: loan, own money, refund, transfer, insurance, other) or cannot tell. The acceptance bar:
- in each Verified stratum, at least 95% of the rows are revenue, and none is a loan, an own-account transfer, owner money or a refund;
- among the 50 largest counted rows, none is a loan, an own-account transfer, owner money or a refund;
- every row that misses the bar gets a named rule, hold or registry entry, with a fabricated test, before merge, and its stratum is re-sampled.

## 15. Out of scope, and the deferred items

- Payer-wide review decisions: OQ1.
- Analyst overrides of rows a non-revenue rule decided. The trace's wrong non-revenue rows are fixed by §7.11. An override would move eligible deposits and the lender-credit exclusion, so it needs its own design. The underwriter's Q11 (b) of 2026-10-02 adds none: an `asset_sale_proceeds` row has no review path until the owner answers §17.1's asset-sale follow-up (2).
- Counting recurrence across statements, accounts or packages.
- The families' open owner items that this spec does not decide. Their rows are counted and flagged (or held, where §8.1 says) until the owner rules:
  - tuition through a payfac (the SV suffix);
  - Applied Systems' agency-bill premium: closed for premium trust accounts by the underwriter's Q10 of 2026-10-02 (§8.10: every corpus row, 68 at c486fd5, sits on the four premium-trust statements and is held there; R2-OW11); outside a premium trust account it reads as before (counted and flagged), and no corpus row exists there;
  - Lyft and individuals' gig income, and Super Dispatch's quick-pay;
  - TikTok creator payouts;
  - tax-preparer fee disbursements and SBTPG;
  - EBT settlements (arm C) and child-care subsidies (CCDF, CACFP);
  - government grants paid as vendor payments;
  - Canadian benefit carriers and the RBC claim label;
  - construction draws and progress billing: the draws ruled 2026-10-02 (the underwriter's Q11 (a): a builder's progress draw counted and flagged, §8.1); `PROGRESS BILLING` stays a deferred source;
  - intercompany invoices;
  - the other accounts-payable items listed at the end of §7.5 (the lease-to-own payers' merchant payouts were ruled by the owner on 2026-10-02, §8.9);
  - property managers' trust money;
  - auction vendor payments and non-dealer consignors, and pairing an auction credit with an equal same-auction debit in the applicant's previous statement (auction risk verifier R9, §7.8). Audit fix batch B8 (I45, §20): the registry's `SECTION_15_DEFERRED_PAYERS` lists the equipment auctions' and the consumer car buyers' seller payouts (Ritchie Bros/RB Global, IronPlanet, Purple Wave, BigIron (audit round 2, R2-B12: R37, §20: as it prints its own name, `BIGIRON` or `BIG IRON AUCTION(S)`, never another `BIG IRON <name>`), GovDeals, Proxibid, `CARVANA PAYOUT`, CarMax but never CarMax Auto Finance, Peddle, Vroom; Copart and IAA only on a seller or consignor word), so Q5 and Q6 never verify them. Ruled 2026-10-02 (the underwriter's Q11 (b), §8.1): on a statement with no dealer evidence their seller payouts are `non_revenue` (`asset_sale_proceeds`, the registry's `ASSET_SALE_PAYERS`); the deferred list itself is unchanged, so a dealer's are still counted and never verified, and Proxibid, which remits the buyers' money to the auction house that ran the sale (the auctioneer's own revenue), stays a deferred source; the auctions' vendor payments and the cross-statement auction pairing stay deferred;
  - whether to admit AppFolio now or hold it with Buildium and Landlord Studio admitted (property evidence verifier R4, T15);
  - eCommission's commission advances.
- The transaction classification of credits, such as Heartland's `TXNS/FEES` credit classified `fee`: revenue is unaffected, and the dashboard shows a credit's revenue tag first.
- Residuals that no printed word can close, recorded for the owner:
  - an unregistered funder that prints a neutral name and a neutral entry (it is counted), including a platform advance paid through Parafin or Pipe before the ledger admits them (§7.3);
  - processor or platform capital paid out inside normal settlements;
  - a Faire retailer's refund;
  - a single-row PayPal push-to-card from a person, verified today by PayPal recurrence;
  - the bank templates that print `ACH CREDIT` on every credit, which verify a lone registry alias (§7.10 closes this for property platforms only).

## 16. Services and rollout

The owner's standing rule applies: one Opus 5.5 implementer per service, then an independent reviewer under the orchestration model policy (`docs/agent-handoffs/ORCHESTRATION-MODEL-POLICY.md`). The orchestrator checks each report's evidence before accepting it.

| # | Service | Owns | Starts after |
|---|---|---|---|
| S1 | Registry and vocabularies | §7.1 to §7.10's registry tables, truncations, `HEALTHCARE_PAYER_ALIASES`, `DEALER_FUNDING_PAYERS`, the validator (§7.4), the ledger admissions of the processors' capital products (§7.1) and of Parafin and Pipe (§7.3) | this spec's approval |
| S2 | Classifier 5.5 | §6.1 steps 3 and 5 to 14 (the channel gate, step 9b, included), statement passes 4 to 6, §5.2's holder test and numbered-company guard, §7.0 to §7.11, the T18 and T19 switches, the 5.5 tests, the version bump | S1 |
| S3 | Census tool | §14.2 and §14.3; runs on 5.4 → 5.5 before S4 starts; the §14.5 sample is drawn from its 5.6 run | S2 |
| S4 | Classifier and payload 5.6 | §6.1 step 4 (Q7), statement pass 7, §5, §8, §9, §11, `analysis/revenue.py`, `metrics.py`, `detect.py`, `serialization.py`, `batch.py`, `analyze.py`, the benchmark, the docs, the version bump | S3's 5.5 report accepted |
| S5 | Webapp serving, package, review and exports | §9.2, §10.4, §10.7, §10.8 | S4's contract (§9); may start on fixtures built from it |
| S6 | Dashboard | §10.1 to §10.3, §10.5, §10.6, §10.7's controls | the same |

- **Order:** S1, then S2, then the 5.5 census (S3), then S4, then S5 and S6 in parallel. Then the 5.6 census, both guard sets, the precision sample (§14.5), the targeted tests, the full suite at the train, and a browser check of the dashboard.
- **Merge and hosting:** the branch merges only after every review closes, the precision sample meets its bar, and the owner has read both census reports and answered OQ5 and OQ6 (without an answer, T18 and T19 ship switched off). The tryout host is not updated unless the owner asks, and its census runs read-only.

## 17. Open questions

The owner has ruled on Q1 to Q8. These are the few left.

- **OQ1. "Apply to every row of this payer."** Recommendation: a follow-up release, not this one.
  - It needs a payer identity that holds across statements and uploads. This spec defines the credit payer key (§5.2), which the follow-up would reuse. It also needs a decisions table keyed by that payer (today's decisions are per job and row), and a rule for when a later statement's row matches.
  - Shipping it inside this release would make the census unmeasurable, because a decision would move rows the rules did not.
  - T7 already cuts the gated share from 95.6% to about 28% to 32%.
- **OQ2. BNPL merchant settlements** (Affirm, Klarna, Afterpay, GreenSky, Sunbit). Should they join `PAYOUT_CREDIT_ENTITIES`, so that their settlements to the merchant are revenue rather than financing proceeds (lender spec D2)? Today they are `non_revenue`. They are rare in the corpus (13 rows).
- **OQ3. Numbered-company payers** (T11: $11.4M, 4.1% of corpus credits, 293 rows). This spec counts them in True, flagged, and never verifies them. Should they be held out until confirmed instead? That would take about 4 points off True.
- **OQ4. The deferred family items of §15.** Each one's rows stay counted and flagged (or held) until you rule. The research folder lists every item with its measured size. Two are new: pairing an auction refund across statements, and admitting AppFolio now or holding it.
- **OQ5. Claim first for an insurer's `HCCLAIMPMT`** (T18). Should a Blue plan's (or any insurer's) healthcare claim payment to a provider verify as revenue, although the insurer registry otherwise makes an insurer's credit non-revenue? Yes moves 177 rows, $908,159, in 16 statements of healthcare providers from `non_revenue` to Verified. No holds them, and the alias-escaping Blue spellings with them, for review.
- **OQ6. Third-party book transfers** (T19). Should Chase's `BOOK TRANSFER CREDIT B O <customer>` and Bank of America's `WIRE TYPE BOOK IN` from someone other than the holder be read as incoming wires, rather than as own-account transfers? Yes moves 308 Chase rows, $6.25M, in 73 statements out of `non_revenue` (into Q5's tiers and holds) and adds one invoice-citing BofA wire ($55,259.05). No keeps both as today.

The owner answered OQ1 to OQ6 at §19.

Alternative: a further decision kind for "this deposit bounced", which the routes, the store and the replay would need.
- **Transfers between the business's accounts: the defaults (the underwriter's Q4 of 2026-10-02, §6.2's package passes; R2-OW16).** Each default is in the code; the owner may change it. (1) The release is Confirm Revenue, one control and one audit trail: it releases the deposit into True and marks it Verified, on its own statement too (§10.7), although a rule never verifies a bare deposit (Q2 of 2026-09-28); the row note says so. Alternative: a release that restores the deposit's earlier counted tier (`tier_before`, which `package_match` already carries), which needs a new decision kind in the route, the store and the replay. (2) A teller, counter or branch deposit stays matchable (a branch transfer between two of the business's accounts can print that way on its receiving side, and the transfer out must still print transfer wording); a check deposit and a deposit printing a cash device's word (ATM, ABM, cash, coin, smart safe, night drop, vault, pre-encoded) or a retail cash load never are. Alternative: refuse every cash, branch and teller form (0 corpus rows either way at c486fd5). A bare `NIGHT DEPOSIT` stays matchable: §8.2's cash form does not read it. (3) A credit whose payer the parser did not read (`payer_text_not_read`) is never matched: such rows are often a welded customer line (R2-B07). Alternative: admit it (0 corpus rows either way). (4) No extra gate: the held deposit gates its statement in the package as any held credit does, and the notice and Held for Review list it. (5) Two accounts of one document are matched too (the owner's example, sent in one PDF, counted twice under R-d, which nets only same-day legs printing a designation). This hold sets no internal-transfer mark and changes no R-d pair, deduction or refusal, so the ruling of 2026-08-30 on R-d's exclusion (L1 design §8.14) is untouched; the corpus holds no multi-account document, so only the tests measure this arm. Alternative: match across uploaded statements only. (6) Two accounts are told apart by their printed numbers alone (four digits or more, the last fours differing or the full numbers conflicting); one account read under two bank spellings is never two, and two banks' accounts sharing a last four are never matched (the conservative direction).
- **Read the printed account number on Chase, Capital One and Banque Royale statements** (the underwriter's Q4 of 2026-10-02; R2-OW16), so the package can check their transfers: a statement whose account number was not read (fewer than four digits) is never paired by Q4 and is marked `no_account_number` ("Transfers between accounts not checked for P statement(s): no account number read"). On the corpus's package proxies (§20) most such statements are Chase's. Parser work, outside this run; Q6 already reaches these accounts through the balance chain, and Q4 follows as soon as the number is read.
- **The Zelle setting: the defaults (the owner's amendment of 2026-10-06 to the underwriter's Q3; §8.4, §9.1, §10.7; R2-OW17).** Each default is in the code; the owner may change it. (1) The Q3-era carve-outs in the counted reading (the orchestrator's choice, 2026-10-06): a Zelle truck or equipment sale is asset-sale proceeds and a builder's Zelle draw counts (Q11 (2026-10-02)), as for Venmo; a Zelle tenant never makes the business a lessor, in both readings, so the setting moves Zelle rows only. Alternatives: keep all three carve-outs (a Zelle `TRUCK SALE` would then count as person-to-person under the default Yes), or lift the lessor's too (a non-Zelle rent `LEASE` would then be released under Yes only, needing its own fact line and export figure). (2) The lender side follows the reading: a bounce-worded Zelle credit the rules count leaves its funder debit paid under Yes (pass 7b; corpus: none). Alternative: pass 7b reads the No reading's tier in both. (3) Analyses stored before the setting are served as analysed, with the True card's notice, until R2-B16's stage bump lets a re-analysis compute both readings. Alternative: a lossy restore from `zelle_prior` (tier and reason right; method, rule, confidence, sentence, the $1 floor, the premium-trust hold and pass 7b wrong). (4) The latest decision on a posting sets every reading, and the replay does the same. Alternative: a decision binds only the reading it was made in (a Yes-mode reject would then vanish on re-analysis unless the review log recorded the mode, a storage schema change). (5) "Flagged 'Zelle'" is the rules' reason plus a row tag (a ledger chip, a `zelle` column) and a True-card line. Alternative: a new counted reason code. (6) The Non-Revenue note keeps ", Zelle deposits included" under No and on a Zelle-free account. Alternative: a top-level mode key on every payload. (7) The benchmark (`benchmark/run.py`, `compare.py`) keeps the stored reading. (8) `zelle_excluded`'s label and sentence are unchanged ("excluded by policy"). (9) One settings file per data directory: everyone using the installation shares the choice, and the gate, the decision pill, the package decision and the withholding rate flip for all of them; a per-underwriter choice waits for sign-in (D-2b).
- **Lender payment changes: the defaults (the owner's request of 2026-10-06, §9.1, §10.1; R2-OW18).** Each default is in the code; the owner may change it. The orchestrator's defaults of 2026-10-06: an increase mirrors the decrease (10% or more, held 2 or more payments; alternative: its own threshold); a schedule change is compared on the weekly equivalent and is never by itself a decrease (alternative: raw amounts); two concurrent positions with one funder are separate series (alternative: one series); the grace windows come from the corpus probe (daily 5, daily irregular 6, weekly 10, biweekly and semi-monthly 15, monthly 25 business days; alternative: other windows); information only (alternative: none). The open points: (1) the increase threshold mirrors the decrease (alternative: 5%, about 10 more increases, mostly variable-pay drift); (2) the statement's items are computed at analysis time (alternative: a serve-time view, which reaches saved jobs but cannot key potential lenders on old payloads); (3) payments are the classification plus the paid flag (alternative: the classification only; measured identical); (4) payloads stored before the check read "not checked" (alternative: compute confirmed series at serve time); (5) the Federal Reserve calendar, and Payments Canada's published closure days on a CAD statement (the Civic Holiday is no closure day; alternative: the US calendar everywhere, which changes the business-day counts of 19 package and 3 statement items and no item's presence); (6) a stop inside one statement is a possible stop (alternative: packages only); (7) temporary cuts and restorations are shown and marked (alternative: suppress a change reverted within N payments); (8) a stream under 5% of the series' weekly weight is a fee stream, dropped (alternatives: raw amounts, or a "fee stream" line); (9) no Settings checkbox (alternative: a display setting); (10) potential lenders are shown in the neutral tone and not under $100 a week (alternatives: amber and blue chips, no or another floor, or no signal on an unnamed key pooling 3 or more streams); (11) the funding note reads a credit from 20 days before to 5 days after the new amount's first payment (alternative: the reverse window, or no note); (12) the statement modal shows its lines but not R2-OW13's returned lines (alternative: both); (13) lines only, no lender-row or ledger chip (alternative: a "Changed" chip); (14) this §2.2 and inline amendments in the lender-detection spec (alternatives: a §2.1 row, no amendment); (15) no cross-reference to R2-OW12's funding aid (alternative: name it); (16) one line per qualifying step of a variable-pay product (alternative: one "variable payment" note per series); (17) a pause that resumes at the same payment is shown (alternative: no line); (18) THE ORCHESTRATOR'S CHOICE OF 2026-10-06, the alternative: a decrease or an increase at a new schedule held 2 payments but not yet the 3 (5 if daily) that confirm it is shown as a possible change, "new schedule not yet confirmed", when it is the position's last regime, or mid-position when its payments span 80% of a cycle (the default showed nothing until confirmed); a possible change never becomes the reference of point 23: the next regime is compared with the last confirmed level, and its line names the possible level and each step in its "via …, then …" suffix (daily 500 → weekly 1,600 held 2 → weekly 2,300 reads a possible -36% decrease, then a schedule change of -8% "via weekly $1,600.00 (-36%), then weekly $2,300.00 (+44%)"; alternative: a possible level becomes the reference; R2-OW18 review round 1); (19) a potential payee's new amount joins its series only once D6 promotes it, 3 equal debits in a statement (alternative: the probe's 'ext' variant, never judged); (20) a bounced payment is presence for pauses, restarts and stops, for every position of its series (alternatives: paid payments only, or the matching position only); a line whose presence is a bounced attempt says so: a pause it ended reads "no payment or payment attempt", names the attempt and the date payments resumed, and a stop whose last presence it is reads "no payment or payment attempt" with the last payment's date (R2-OW18 review round 1; on the corpus 1 package and 1 statement pause and 4 package stops); (21) an amount change whose old and new amounts overlap for a few payments reads as a stop with "another … payment stream continues" (alternative: an "overlapping" change); (22) a level at 2x or 3x the main amount never run longer than 2 payments is a catch-up (alternative: only when the main level returns); (23) THE ORCHESTRATOR'S CHOICE OF 2026-10-06, the alternative: each regime is compared with the last REPORTED level of its position (the first level until something is reported), so steps under 10% that add up are reported once the cumulative change reaches 10% (the default compared each regime with the one before it); such a line names the unreported levels with the step into each and the last step ("via weekly $950.00 (-5%), then weekly $650.00 (-32%)"), never "steps of under 10% each": an abrupt last step after a small drift reads as such (R2-OW18 review round 1; on the corpus 9 of the 12 package and 1 of the 2 statement lines with such levels have a step of 10% or more); (24) one presence definition, payments, attempts and payment-sized one-offs of 5% to under 2x (alternative: the probe's); a restart's pause, like a pause, leaves out the business days no statement of the chain covers (a hole between two members), so a level change across a hole is no restart unless the covered days alone pass the grace (R2-OW18 review round 1; no corpus item moves); (25) a funder that moves to another account of the deal is never a confirmed stop (alternative: chains only); (26) a second stream that raises the weekly total by 10% or more is a "New payment stream" (alternative: no line); a stream whose payment one cycle of its schedule before its first one would fall before the covered period or in a hole between two statements is no new stream, since it may have been paying before (R2-OW18 review round 1: 3 of the 10 confirmed package new streams leave, each monthly and first paid 25 or 26 days into its chain; alternative: B8 as the brief wrote it); (27) the confirmed chip reads "No payments", and a stop names a debt relief program and a new lender series (alternatives: "Stopped", no such notes); (28) a stop is confirmed only by later statements covering 80% of a cycle (alternative: any later statement); (29) a known false shape (R2-OW18 review round 1): levels read each debit, never a day's sum, so a funder's payment taken as two debits on one day reads as a change of level and a change back (750 + 750 in place of one 1,500 is a -50% decrease, then +100% when the single debit returns; 1,000 + 500 a decrease beside a new stream); on the corpus 288 of 1,740 confirmed statement series have two payments on one day, and the split shape sits behind 2 package increases and 1 statement increase (alternative: sum a series' same-day payments before reading its levels, which would also merge two concurrent streams paid on one day). Points 18 to 29 narrow or extend the owner's words or add a review's rule; §20 gives their measured cost.

It simulated 48 fabricated rows against the draft (`work/spec/review/sim_review.py`, private) and found five critical and eleven important problems, plus twelve minor ones. This revision applies every critical and important finding and every minor one. The holds and sizes the review asked to re-measure were re-measured on the memo's rows (`work/spec/revision/revision_probe.py`, private; totals only).
